[Contains English characters] आद्य द्राविडीयन भाषा Proto-Dravidian is the proto-language of the Dravidian languages.
[Contains English characters] Proto-languages are, by definition, hypothetical languages reconstructed by linguists, and hence no proto-language has any historical record.
[Contains English characters] So is the case with Proto-Dravidian.
[Contains English characters] Due to a dearth of comparative linguistic research into the Dravidian languages, not many details as to the grammar, epoch, or location of Proto-Dravidian are known.
[Contains English characters] It is thought to have differentiated into Proto-North Dravidian, Proto-Central Dravidian and Proto-South Dravidian around 500 BC, although some linguists have argued that the degree of differentiation between the sub-families points to an earlier split.
[Contains English characters] The only book which covers all the Dravidian languages which can point to Proto-Dravidian forms is Dravidian Etymological Dictionary still consist only of lists of related words without further explanation; therefore for a talented linguist Proto-Dravidian offers large possibilities.
[Contains English characters] Here we discuss the salient features of the reconstructed Proto-Dravidian language.
[Contains English characters] Vowels: Proto-Dravidian contrasted between five short and long vowels: *a, *ā, *i, *ī, *u, *ū, *e, *ē, *o, *ō.
[Contains English characters] The sequences *ai and *au are treated as *ay and *av Consonants: Proto-Dravidian is reconstructible with the following consonantal phonemes : The alveolar stop *ṯ in many daughter languages developed into an alveolar trill /r/.
[Contains English characters] The stop sound is retained in Kota and Toda .
[Contains English characters] Malayalam still retains the original stop sound in gemination. . In Old Tamil it took the enunciative vowel like the other stops.
[Contains English characters] In other words, *ṯ did not occur word-finally without the enunciative vowel .
[Contains English characters] Velar nasal *ṅ occurred only before *k in Proto-Dravidian .
[Contains English characters] Therefore it is not considered a separate phoneme in Proto-Dravidian.
[Contains English characters] However, it attained phonemic status in languages like Malayalam, Gondi, Konda and Pengo due to the simplification of the original sequence *ṅk to *ṅ.
[Contains English characters] The glottal fricative *h has been proposed by Bh.
[Contains English characters] Krishnamurthi to account for the Old Tamil Aytam and other Dravidian comparative phonological phenomena .
[Contains English characters] The Dravidian languages have been found mainly in South India since the start of the common era.
[Contains English characters] Speculations regarding the original homeland being a mythical sunken continent called Kumari Kandam, or the Indus Valley Civilization are largely discredited in academic circles to Dravidian languages especially to Telugu needs to be explained.
[Contains English characters] Iravatham Mahadevan, who with his knowledge of both Tamil and Sanskrit, spent many decades studying the IVC script said in an interview in 1998 that IVC script is undeciphered.
[Contains English characters] According to Michael Witzel, the well-known Indologist, there are not many Dravidian loan words in the earliest stratum of Vedas, even though, the Dravidian influence quickly increases in the post-Rigvedic period.

[Contains English characters] However, unlike Hollywood, Bollywood does not exist as a physical place.

[Contains English characters] The term Bollywood has origins in the 1970s, when India overtook America as the worlds largest film producer.
[Contains English characters] Credit for the term has been claimed by several different people, including the lyricist, filmmaker and scholar Amit Khanna, and the journalist Bevinda Collaco.
[Contains English characters] The naming scheme for Bollywood was inspired by Tollywood, the name that was used to refer to the cinema of West Bengal.
[Contains English characters] Dating back to 1932, Tollywood was the earliest Hollywood-inspired name, referring to the Bengali film industry based in Tollygunge, which rhymed with Hollywood and was the center of the cinema of India at the time.
[Contains English characters] The name Bollywood later arose as the Bombay-based film industry overtook the one in Tollygunge as the center of the Indian film industry.
[Contains English characters] The 1930s and 1940s were tumultuous times: India was buffeted by the Great Depression, World War II, the Indian independence movement, and the violence of the Partition.
[Contains English characters] Most Bollywood films were unabashedly escapist, but there were also a number of filmmakers who tackled tough social issues, or used the struggle for Indian independence as a backdrop for their plots.
[Contains English characters] In 1937, Ardeshir Irani, of Alam Ara fame, made the first colour film in Hindi, Kisan Kanya.
[Contains English characters] The next year, he made another colour film, Mother India.
[Contains English characters] However, colour did not become a popular feature until the late 1950s.
[Contains English characters] At this time, lavish romantic musicals and melodramas were the staple fare at the cinema.
[Contains English characters] Following Indias independence, the period from the late 1940s to the 1960s are regarded by film historians as the Golden Age of Hindi cinema.
[Contains English characters] Some of the most critically-acclaimed Hindi films of all time were produced during this period.
[Contains English characters] Examples include the Guru Dutt films Pyaasa and Kaagaz Ke Phool and the Raj Kapoor films Awaara and Shree 420 .
[Contains English characters] These films expressed social themes mainly dealing with working-class urban life in India; Awaara presented the city as both a nightmare and a dream, while Pyaasa critiqued the unreality of city life.
[Contains English characters] Some of the most famous epic films of Hindi cinema were also produced at the time, including Mehboob Khans Mother India, which was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, and K.
[Contains English characters] Asifs Mughal-e-Azam . V. Shantarams Do Aankhen Barah Haath is believed to have inspired the Hollywood film The Dirty Dozen .
[Contains English characters] Madhumati, directed by Bimal Roy and written by Ritwik Ghatak, popularized the theme of reincarnation in Western popular culture.
[Contains English characters] Other acclaimed mainstream Hindi filmmakers at the time included Kamal Amrohi and Vijay Bhatt.
[Contains English characters] Successful actors at the time included Dev Anand, Dilip Kumar, Raj Kapoor and Guru Dutt, while successful actresses included Nargis, Meena Kumari, Nutan, Madhubala, Waheeda Rehman and Mala Sinha.
[Contains English characters] While commercial Hindi cinema was thriving, the 1950s also saw the emergence of a new Parallel Cinema movement.
[Contains English characters] Though the movement was mainly led by Bengali cinema, it also began gaining prominence in Hindi cinema.
[Contains English characters] Early examples of Hindi films in this movement include Chetan Anands Neecha Nagar and Bimal Roys Two Acres of Land .
[Contains English characters] Their critical acclaim, as well as the latters commercial success, paved the way for Indian neorealism and the Indian New Wave.
[Contains English characters] Some of the internationally-acclaimed Hindi filmmakers involved in the movement included Mani Kaul, Kumar Shahani, Ketan Mehta, Govind Nihalani, Shyam Benegal and Vijaya Mehta.
[Contains English characters] Ever since the social realist film Neecha Nagar won the Grand Prize at the first Cannes Film Festival, Hindi films were frequently in competition for the Palme dOr at the Cannes Film Festival throughout the 1950s and early 1960s, with some of them winning major prizes at the festival.
[Contains English characters] Guru Dutt, while overlooked in his own lifetime, had belatedly generated international recognition much later in the 1980s.
[Contains English characters] Dutt is now regarded as one of the greatest Asian filmmakers of all time, alongside the more famous Indian Bengali filmmaker Satyajit Ray.

[Contains English characters] Bollywood films are mostly musicals, and are expected to contain catchy music in the form of song-and-dance numbers woven into the script.
[Contains English characters] A films success often depends on the quality of such musical numbers.
[Contains English characters] Indeed, a films music is often released before the movie itself and helps increase the audience.
[Contains English characters] Indian audiences expect full value for their money, with a good entertainer generally referred to as paisa vasool, .
[Contains English characters] Songs and dances, love triangles, comedy and dare-devil thrills are all mixed up in a three-hour-long extravaganza with an intermission.
[Contains English characters] Such movies are called masala films, after the Hindi word for a spice mixture.
[Contains English characters] Like masalas, these movies are a mixture of many things such as action, comedy, romance etc.
[Contains English characters] Most films have heroes who are able to fight off villains all by themselves.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood plots have tended to be melodramatic.
[Contains English characters] They frequently employ formulaic ingredients such as star-crossed lovers and angry parents, love triangles, family ties, sacrifice, corrupt politicians, kidnappers, conniving villains, courtesans with hearts of gold, long-lost relatives and siblings separated by fate, dramatic reversals of fortune, and convenient coincidences.
[Contains English characters] There have always been Indian films with more artistic aims and more sophisticated stories, both inside and outside the Bollywood tradition .
[Contains English characters] They often lost out at the box office to movies with more mass appeal.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood conventions are changing, however.
[Contains English characters] A large Indian diaspora in English speaking countries, and increased Western influence at home, have nudged Bollywood films closer to Hollywood models.

[Contains English characters] Plots now tend to feature Westernised urbanites dating and dancing in clubs rather than centering on pre-arranged marriages.
[Contains English characters] Though these changes can widely be seen in contemporary Bollywood, traditional conservative ways of Indian culture continue to exist in India outside the industry and an element of resistance by some to western-based influences.
[Contains English characters] Despite this, Bollywood continues to play a major role in fashion in India.
[Contains English characters] Indeed some studies into fashion in India have revealed that some people are unaware that the changing nature of fashion in Bollywood films which are presented to them are often influenced by globalisation and many consider the clothes worn by Bollywood actors as authentically Indian.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood employs people from all parts of India.
[Contains English characters] It attracts thousands of aspiring actors and actresses, all hoping for a break in the industry.
[Contains English characters] Models and beauty contestants, television actors, theatre actors and even common people come to Mumbai with the hope and dream of becoming a star.
[Contains English characters] Just as in Hollywood, very few succeed.
[Contains English characters] Since many Bollywood films are shot abroad, many foreign extras are employed too.
[Contains English characters] Stardom in the entertainment industry is very fickle, and Bollywood is no exception.
[Contains English characters] The popularity of the stars can rise and fall rapidly.
[Contains English characters] Directors compete to hire the most popular stars of the day, who are believed to guarantee the success of a movie .
[Contains English characters] Hence many stars make the most of their fame, once they become popular, by making several movies simultaneously.
[Contains English characters] Only a very few non-Indian actors are able to make a mark in Bollywood, though many have tried from time to time.

[Contains English characters] Kisna, Lagaan, and The Rising: Ballad of Mangal Pandey also featured foreign actors.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood can be very clannish, and the relatives of film-industry insiders have an edge in getting coveted roles in films or being part of a films crew.
[Contains English characters] Industry connections are no guarantee of a long career: competition is fierce and if film industry scions do not succeed at the box office, their careers will falter.
[Contains English characters] Some of the biggest stars, such as Dharmendra, Amitabh Bachchan, and Shahrukh Khan have succeeded despite total lack of show business connections.

[Contains English characters] Process known as looping in the sound or ADR—with the foley and sound effects added later.
[Contains English characters] This creates several problems, since the sound in these films usually occurs a frame or two earlier or later than the mouth movements or gestures.
[Contains English characters] The actors have to act twice: once on-location, once in the studio—and the emotional level on set is often very difficult to recreate.
[Contains English characters] Commercial Indian films, not just the Hindi-language variety, are known for their lack of ambient sound, so there is a silence underlying everything instead of the background sound and noises usually employed in films to create aurally perceivable depth and environment.
[Contains English characters] The ubiquity of ADR in Bollywood cinema became prevalent in the early 1960s with the arrival of the Arriflex 3 camera, which required a blimp in order to shield the sound of the camera, for which it was notorious, from on-location filming.
[Contains English characters] Commercial Indian filmmakers, known for their speed, never bothered to blimp the camera, and its excessive noise required that everything had to be recreated in the studio.
[Contains English characters] Eventually, this became the standard for Indian films.
[Contains English characters] The trend was bucked in 2001, after a 30-year hiatus of synchronized sound, with the film Lagaan, in which producer-star Aamir Khan insisted that the sound be done on location.
[Contains English characters] This opened up a heated debate on the use and economic feasibility of on-location sound, and several Bollywood films have employed on-location sound since then.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood film music is called filmi music .
[Contains English characters] Songs from Bollywood movies are generally pre-recorded by professional playback singers, with the actors then lip synching the words to the song on-screen, often while dancing.
[Contains English characters] While most actors, especially today, are excellent dancers, few are also singers.
[Contains English characters] One notable exception was Kishore Kumar, who starred in several major films in the 1950s while also having a stellar career as a playback singer. K. L. Saigal, Suraiyya, and Noor Jehan were also known as both singers and actors.
[Contains English characters] Some actors in the last thirty years have sung one or more songs themselves; for a list, see Singing actors and actresses in Indian cinema.
[Contains English characters] Playback singers are prominently featured in the opening credits and have their own fans who will go to an otherwise lackluster movie just to hear their favourites.
[Contains English characters] Going by the quality as well as the quantity of the songs they rendered, most notable singers of Bollywood are Lata Mangeshkar, Asha Bhosle, Geeta Dutt, Shamshad Begum and Alka Yagnik among female playback singers; and K. L. Saigal, Talat Mahmood, Mukesh, Mohammed Rafi, Manna Dey, Hemant Kumar, Kishore Kumar, Kumar Sanu, S.

[Contains English characters] Mohammed Rafi is often considered arguably the finest of the singers that have lent their voice to Bollywood songs, followed by Lata Mangeshkar, who, through the course of a career spanning over six decades, has recorded thousands of songs for Indian movies.
[Contains English characters] The composers of film music, known as music directors, are also well-known.
[Contains English characters] Their songs can make or break a film and usually do.
[Contains English characters] Remixing of film songs with modern beats and rhythms is a common occurrence today, and producers may even release remixed versions of some of their films songs along with the films regular soundtrack albums.
[Contains English characters] The dancing in Bollywood films, especially older ones, is primarily modelled on Indian dance: classical dance styles, dances of historic northern Indian courtesans, or folk dances.
[Contains English characters] In modern films, Indian dance elements often blend with Western dance styles, though it is not unusual to see Western pop and pure classical dance numbers side by side in the same film.
[Contains English characters] The hero or heroine will often perform with a troupe of supporting dancers.
[Contains English characters] Many song-and-dance routines in Indian films feature unrealistically instantaneous shifts of location or changes of costume between verses of a song.
[Contains English characters] If the hero and heroine dance and sing a pas de deux, it is often staged in beautiful natural surroundings or architecturally grand settings.
[Contains English characters] This staging is referred to as a picturisation.
[Contains English characters] Songs typically comment on the action taking place in the movie, in several ways.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes, a song is worked into the plot, so that a character has a reason to sing; other times, a song is an externalisation of a characters thoughts, or presages an event that has not occurred yet in the plot of the movie.
[Contains English characters] In this case, the event is almost always two characters falling in love.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood films have always used what are now called item numbers.
[Contains English characters] A physically attractive female character, often completely unrelated to the main cast and plot of the film, performs a catchy song and dance number in the film.
[Contains English characters] In older films, the item number may be performed by a courtesan dancing for a rich client or as part of a cabaret show.
[Contains English characters] The dancer Helen was famous for her cabaret numbers.
[Contains English characters] In modern films, item numbers may be inserted as discotheque sequences, dancing at celebrations, or as stage shows.
[Contains English characters] For the last few decades Bollywood producers have been releasing the films soundtrack, as tapes or CDs, before the main movie release, hoping that the music will pull audiences into the cinema later.
[Contains English characters] Often the soundtrack is more popular than the movie.
[Contains English characters] In the last few years some producers have also been releasing music videos, usually featuring a song from the film.
[Contains English characters] However, some promotional videos feature a song which is not included in the movie.
[Contains English characters] The film script or lines of dialogue and the song lyrics are often written by different people.
[Contains English characters] Dialogues are usually written in an unadorned Hindi or Hindustani that would be understood by the largest possible audience.
[Contains English characters] Some movies, however, have used regional dialects to evoke a village setting, or old-fashioned courtly उर्दू भाषा in Mughal era historical films.
[Contains English characters] Contemporary mainstream movies also make great use of English.
[Contains English characters] Some movie scripts are first written in Roman alphabet.
[Contains English characters] Characters may shift from one language to the other to express a certain atmosphere .
[Contains English characters] Cinematic language, whether in dialogues or lyrics, is often melodramatic and invokes God, family, mother, duty, and self-sacrifice liberally.
[Contains English characters] Music directors often prefer working with certain lyricists, to the point that the lyricist and composer are seen as a team.
[Contains English characters] This phenomenon is not unlike the pairings of American composers and songwriters that created old-time Broadway musicals .
[Contains English characters] Song lyrics are usually about love.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood song lyrics, especially in the old movies, frequently use Arabo-Persic Urdu vocabulary.
[Contains English characters] Another source for love lyrics is the long Hindu tradition of poetry about the mythological amours of Krishna, Radha, and the gopis.
[Contains English characters] Many lyrics compare the singer to a devotee and the object of his or her passion to Krishna or Radha.
[Contains English characters] Bollywood films are multi-million dollar productions, with the most expensive productions costing up to 100 crores rupees .
[Contains English characters] Sets, costumes, special effects, and cinematography were less than world-class up until the mid-to-late 1990s, although with some notable exceptions.
[Contains English characters] As Western films and television gain wider distribution in India itself, there is an increasing pressure for Bollywood films to attain the same production levels, particularly in areas such as action and special effects.
[Contains English characters] Recent Bollywood films have employed international technicians to improve in these areas, such as Krrish which has action choreographed by Hong Kong based Tony Ching.
[Contains English characters] The increasing accessibility to professional action and special effects, coupled with rising film budgets, has seen an explosion in the action and sci-fi genres.

[Contains English characters] Indian banks and financial institutions were forbidden from lending money to movie studios.
[Contains English characters] However, this ban has now been lifted.
[Contains English characters] As finances are not regulated, some funding also comes from illegitimate sources, such as the Mumbai underworld.

[Contains English characters] Another problem facing Bollywood is widespread copyright infringement of its films.
[Contains English characters] Often, bootleg DVD copies of movies are available before the prints are officially released in cinemas.
[Contains English characters] Manufacturing of bootleg DVD, VCD, and VHS copies of the latest movie शीर्षकs is a well established small scale industry in parts of South Asia and South East Asia.
[Contains English characters] The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry estimates that the Bollywood industry loses $100 million annually in loss of revenue from pirated home videos and DVDs.

[Contains English characters] The availability of illegal copies of movies on the Internet also contributes to the piracy problem.

[Contains English characters] The Filmfare Awards ceremony is one of the most prominent film events given for Hindi films in India.
[Contains English characters] The Indian screen magazine Filmfare started the first Filmfare Awards in 1954, and awards were given to the best films of 1953. The ceremony was referred to as the Clare Awards after the magazines editor.
[Contains English characters] Modelled after the poll-based merit format of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, individuals may submit their votes in separate categories.
[Contains English characters] A dual voting system was developed in 1956. Like the Oscars, the Filmfare awards are frequently accused of bias towards commercial success rather than artistic merit.
[Contains English characters] As the Filmfare, the National Film Awards were introduced in 1954. Since 1973, the Indian government has sponsored the National Film Awards, awarded by the government run Directorate of Film Festivals .
[Contains English characters] The DFF screens not only Bollywood films, but films from all the other regional movie industries and independent/art films.
[Contains English characters] These awards are handed out at an annual ceremony presided over by the President of India.
[Contains English characters] Under this system, in contrast to the National Film Awards, which are decided by a panel appointed by Indian Government, the Filmfare Awards are voted for by both the public and a committee of experts.

[Contains English characters] Constrained by rushed production schedules and small budgets, some Bollywood writers and musicians have been known to resort to plagiarism.
[Contains English characters] Ideas, plot lines, tunes or riffs have been copied from other Indian film industries or foreign films .
[Contains English characters] This has led to criticism towards the film industry.
[Contains English characters] In past times, this could be done with impunity.
[Contains English characters] Copyright enforcement was lax in India and few actors or directors ever saw an official contract.
[Contains English characters] The Hindi film industry was not widely known to non-Indian audiences, who would not even be aware that their material was being copied.
[Contains English characters] Audiences may also not have been aware of the plagiarism since many audiences in India were unfamiliar with foreign films and music.
[Contains English characters] While copyright enforcement in India is still somewhat lenient, Bollywood and other film industries are much more aware of each other now and Indian audiences are more familiar with foreign movies and music.
[Contains English characters] Organizations like the India EU Film Initiative seek to foster a community between film makers and industry professional between India and the EU.
[Contains English characters] One of the common justifications of plagiarism in Bollywood is that producers often play a safer option by remaking popular Hollywood films in an Indian context.
[Contains English characters] Screenwriters generally produce original scripts, but due to financial uncertainty and insecurity over the success of a film many were rejected.
[Contains English characters] Screenwriters themselves have been criticised for lack of creativity which happened due to tight schedules and restricted funds in the industry to employ better screenwriters.
[Contains English characters] Certain filmmakers see plagiarism in Bollywood as an integral part of globalisation where American and western cultures are firmly embedding themselves into Indian culture, which is manifested, amongst other mediums, in Bollywood films.

[Contains English characters] Riot laws: Riot Act, Black Act Under English law, a riot is defined by the Public Order Act 1986 as twelve or more persons who together use or threaten unlawful violence for a common purpose and the conduct of them is such as would cause a person of reasonable firmness present at the scene to fear for his personal safety.
[Contains English characters] A single person can be liable for an offense of riot when they use violence provided that it can be shown there were at least twelve present using or threatening violence.
[Contains English characters] The violence can be against the person or against property.
[Contains English characters] This carries the possibility of a fine and a sentence of up to ten years imprisonment.
[Contains English characters] If there are fewer than twelve people present, the lesser offense of Violent Disorder is charged, for which there is a requirement for at least three persons to use or threaten unlawful violence together.
[Contains English characters] This is defined similarly to riot, but no common purpose is required.
[Contains English characters] In the past, The Riot Act had to be read by an official - with the wording exactly correct - before any policing action could take place.
[Contains English characters] If the group did not disperse after the act was read, lethal force could legally be used against the crowd.
[Contains English characters] In recent times nobody has been charged with a Section 1 offense in England and Wales.
[Contains English characters] This is because if a Section 1 offense takes place the local police service are regarded as having failed and are liable to pay compensation.
[Contains English characters] The best known example of this is the Poll tax demonstrations of 1990 where nobody was charged with Section 1. All were charged as though a collection of Section 2 acts had just happened to take place in one location.
[Contains English characters] In English Law Riot forms part of the Public Order Act 1986 under section 1. The Public Order Act 1986 s.
[Contains English characters] 1 states: 1 Where twelve or more persons who are present together use or threaten unlawful violence for a common purpose and the conduct of them is such as would cause a person of reasonable firmness present at the scene to fear for his personal safety, each of the persons using unlawful violence for the common purpose is guilty of riot.
[Contains English characters] 2 It is immaterial whether or not the twelve or more use or threaten unlawful violence simultaneously.
[Contains English characters] 3 The common purpose may be inferred from conduct.
[Contains English characters] 4 No person of reasonable firmness need actually be, or be likely to be, present at the scene.
[Contains English characters] 5 Riot may be committed in private as well as in public places.
[Contains English characters] Under United States federal law, a riot is defined as A public disturbance involving an act or acts of violence by one or more persons part of an assemblage of three or more persons, which act or acts shall constitute a clear and present danger of, or shall result in, damage or injury to the property of any other person or to the person of any other individual or a threat or threats of the commission of an act or acts of violence by one or more persons part of an assemblage of three or more persons having, individually or collectively, the ability of immediate execution of such threat or threats, where the performance of the threatened act or acts of violence would constitute a clear and present danger of, or would result in, damage or injury to the property of any other person or to the person of any other individual. साचा:Usc. [Contains English characters] A transfer dump is a standard dump truck which pulls a separate trailer which can also be loaded with aggregate The second aggregate container, on the trailer, is powered by either an electric, pneumatic motor or hydraulic line,.
[Contains English characters] It rolls on small wheels, riding on rails from the trailers frame, into the empty main dump box.
[Contains English characters] This maximizes payload capacity without sacrificing the maneuverability of the standard dump truck.
[Contains English characters] Transfer dumps are typically seen in the western United States because of the peculiar weight restrictions on western highways.
[Contains English characters] Another configuration seen is called a Triple Transfer Train, which consists of a B and C box.
[Contains English characters] These are common on Nevada and Utah Highways but not in California.
[Contains English characters] Depending on the axle arrangement, a Triple Transfer can haul up to 129,000 grams with a special permit in certain US states.
[Contains English characters] The Triple Transfer usually costs a contactor about $105 an hour while a A/B config usually runs about $85 per hour .
[Contains English characters] Transfer dump trucks typically haul between 26 and 27 tons of aggregate per load, each truck is capable of 3-5 loads per day, generally speaking.
[Contains English characters] A truck and pup is very similar to a transfer dump.
[Contains English characters] It consists of a standard dump truck pulling a dump trailer.
[Contains English characters] The pup trailer, unlike the transfer, has its own hydraulic ram and is capable of self-unloading.
[Contains English characters] A Superdump is a straight dump truck equipped with a trailing axle, a liftable, load-bearing axle rated as high as 13,000 pounds.
[Contains English characters] Trailing 11 to १३ फूट behind the rear tandem, the trailing axle stretches the outer bridge measurement—the distance between the first and last axles—to the maximum overall length allowed.
[Contains English characters] This increases the gross weight allowed under the federal bridge formula, which sets standards for truck size and weight.
[Contains English characters] Depending on the vehicle length and axle configuration, Superdumps can be rated as high as 80,000 pounds GVW and carry 26 tons of payload or more.
[Contains English characters] When the truck is empty or ready to offload, the trailing axle toggles up off the road surface on two hydraulic arms to clear the rear of the vehicle.
[Contains English characters] Truck owners call their trailing axle-equipped trucks Superdumps because they far exceed the payload, productivity, and return on investment of a conventional dump truck.
[Contains English characters] The Superdump and trailing axle concept was developed by Strong Industries of Houston, Texas.
[Contains English characters] A semi end dump is a tractor-trailer combination wherein the trailer itself contains the hydraulic hoist.
[Contains English characters] A typical semi end dump has a 3-axle tractor pulling a 2-axle semi-trailer.
[Contains English characters] The key advantage of a semi end dump is rapid unloading.
[Contains English characters] A key disadvantage is that they are very unstable when raised in the dumping position limiting their use in many applications where the dumping location is uneven or off level.
[Contains English characters] A semi bottom dump is a 3-axle tractor pulling a 2-axle trailer with a clam shell type dump gate in the belly of the trailer.
[Contains English characters] The key advantage of a semi bottom dump is its ability to lay material in a wind row .
[Contains English characters] In addition, a semi bottom dump is maneuverable in reverse, unlike the double and triple trailer configurations described below.
[Contains English characters] These trailers may be found either of the windrow type shown in the photo, or may be of the cross spread type with the gates opening front to rear instead of left and right.
[Contains English characters] The cross spread gates will actually spread gravel fairly evenly the width of the trailer.
[Contains English characters] by comparison, the windrow gates leave a pile in the middle.
[Contains English characters] The cross spreads jam and do not work well with larger materials.
[Contains English characters] Likewise they are not suitable for use where spreading is not desired such as when hot asphalt paving material is being dumped in front of a paving machine.
[Contains English characters] Double and triple bottom dumps consist of a 2-axle tractor pulling one single-axle semi-trailer and an additional full trailer .
[Contains English characters] These dump trucks allow the driver to lay material in windrows without leaving the cab or stopping the truck.
[Contains English characters] The main disadvantage is the difficulty in backing double and triple units.
[Contains English characters] The specific type of dump truck used in any specific country is likely to be closely keyed to the weight and axle limitations of that jurisdiction.
[Contains English characters] Rock, dirt and other types of materials commonly hauled in trucks of this type are quite heavy, and almost any style of truck can be easily overloaded.
[Contains English characters] Because of this, this type of truck is frequently configured to take advantage of local weight limitations to maximize the cargo.
[Contains English characters] For example, within the United States, the maximum weight limit of 40 tons throughout the country, except for specific bridges with lower limits.
[Contains English characters] Individual states, in some instances, are allowed to authorize trucks up to 52.5 tons.
[Contains English characters] Most states that do so require that the trucks be very long, to spread the weight over more distance.
[Contains English characters] It is in this context that double and triple bottoms are found within the US.
[Contains English characters] A side dump truck consists of a 3-axle tractor pulling a 2-axle semi-trailer.
[Contains English characters] It has hydraulic rams which tilt the dump body onto its side, spilling the material to either the left or right side of the trailer.
[Contains English characters] The key advantages of the side dump are that it allows rapid unloading and can carry more weight in western United States.
[Contains English characters] In addition, it is almost immune to upset while dumping unlike the semi end dumps which are very prone to tipping over.
[Contains English characters] It is, however, highly likely that a side dump trailer will tip over if dumping is stopped prematurely.
[Contains English characters] Also, when dumping lose materials or cobble sized stone, the side dump can become stuck if the pile becomes wide enough to cover too much of the trailers wheels.
[Contains English characters] Trailers that dump at the appropriate angle avoid the problem of the dumped load fouling the path of the trailer wheels by dumping their loads further to the side of the truck, in some cases leaving sufficient clearance to walk between the dumped load and the trailer.
[Contains English characters] Off-road dump trucks more closely resemble heavy construction equipment or engineering vehicles than they do highway dump trucks.
[Contains English characters] They are used strictly off-road for mining and heavy dirt hauling jobs.
[Contains English characters] The term ‘Dump’ Truck is not generally used by the mining industry, or by the manufacturers that build these machines.
[Contains English characters] The more appropriate US term for this strictly off road vehicle is, ‘Haul’ truck and the equivalent European term is Dumper.
[Contains English characters] The classification bottom and side for example, describes how the loaded material is discharged once loaded.
[Contains English characters] In the case of the Haul truck illustrated, a Liebherr T 282B the load is discharged to the rear, designating this particular vehicle as an end dump.
[Contains English characters] Bottom dump normally describes a trailer that discharges its load by opening two clam shell doors under the load space, in some examples several trailers are pulled by one truck mainly these are on road machines.
[Contains English characters] The only remaining example of what is described as a unitized bottom dump coal hauler is manufactured by Kress Corporation.
[Contains English characters] This large capacity truck is used for the transportation of coal from a loading device directly to a power station or bulk storage area.
[Contains English characters] The current largest off road haul trucks are the Liebherr T282B and the Caterpillar 797F, which both have payloads of 400 short tons.
[Contains English characters] Even though these trucks are similar in capacity the Caterpillar is referred to as a mechanical truck since it uses a C175-20 20 cylinder diesel and big transmissions to power the rear wheels.
[Contains English characters] The Liebherr is referred to as a Diesel-Electric Truck since it uses a diesel engine linked to an alternator that generates electricity which is converted to AC used to power two giant electric motors found on the rear wheel assemblies, similar to a locomotive .
[Contains English characters] Besides Liebherr and Caterpillar, Hitachi, Terex, Komatsu and others also fabricate such off road haul trucks in different capacities.
[Contains English characters] Dump trucks are normally built for some amount of off-road or construction site driving; as the driver is protected by the chassis and height of the drivers seat, bumpers are either placed high or omitted for added ground clearance.
[Contains English characters] The disadvantage is that in a collision with a standard car, the entire motor section or luggage compartment goes under the truck.
[Contains English characters] Thus, passengers in the car could be more severely injured than would be common in a collision with another car.
[Contains English characters] Several countries have made rules that new trucks should have bumpers approximately ४० सेंमी above ground in order to protect other drivers better.
[Contains English characters] There are also rules about how long the load or construction of the truck can go beyond the rear bumper to prevent cars that rear-end the truck from going under it.

[Contains English characters] The Pallava dynasty was a Tamil dynasty of South India which ruled the northern Tamil Nadu region and whole of Andhra Pradesh with their capital at Kanchipuram.
[Contains English characters] The word Pallava in Sanskrit means branch.
[Contains English characters] The Pallava dynasty is an offshoot of the Chola rulers .
[Contains English characters] They expanded into the Guntur region of Andhra Pradesh.
[Contains English characters] This area is still referred to as Palnadu or Pallava Nadu.
[Contains English characters] Pallavas gained prominence after the eclipse of Satavahanas of Andhra and decline of Cholas in Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas patronized Tamil, Telugu and Sanskrit.
[Contains English characters] Some of the most illustrious Sanskrit poets like Bharavi and Dandin and the seashore rock-cut temples of Mahabalipuram belongs to the Pallavan era.
[Contains English characters] Pallavas rose in power during the reign of Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I and dominated the Telugu and northern parts of the Tamil region for about six hundred years until the end of the 9th century.
[Contains English characters] Throughout their reign they were in constant conflict with both Chalukyas of Badami in the north and the Tamil kingdoms of Chola and Pandyas in the south and were finally defeated by the Chola kings in the 8th century CE.
[Contains English characters] Pallavas are most noted for their patronage of architecture, still seen today in Mahabalipuram.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas, who left behind magnificent sculptures and temples, established the foundations of medieval south Indian architecture.
[Contains English characters] Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang visited Kanchipuram during Pallava rule and extolled their benign rule.
[Contains English characters] Many sources describe Bodhidharma, the founder of the Zen school of Buddhism in China, as a prince of the Pallava dynasty, a contemporary of Skandavarman IV and Nandivarman I, and the son of Simhavarman II, though this is debatable.
[Contains English characters] The word Pallava means branch in Sanskrit, in contrast with Chola meaning new country, Pandiya meaning old country and Chera meaning hill country in Sangam Tamil lexicon.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas are considered to be later offshoot of Cholas, who made Kanchipuram their capital and ruled Northern Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh .
[Contains English characters] They have also conquered Southern Karnataka.
[Contains English characters] The origins of the Pallavas are shrouded in myths and legends.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas are described to belong to the line of sage Bharadwaja.
[Contains English characters] Aswattama the son of Drona once while being in a hermitage near the province of Funan in South-East Asia was visited upon by the celestial nymph called Menaka who sought his hand.
[Contains English characters] The child that they begot was called Pallava.
[Contains English characters] Several grants recollect this by seeing Pallavas valour to be equal to that of Aswattaman who that night of war relentlessly fought the demonic army of Ghatotgacha the son of Bheema.
[Contains English characters] This apart several Pallavas were praised to have mastered and practiced alongside arms, the agamic worship rituals .
[Contains English characters] This apart the Pallava insignia of mace Khatvanga of Lord Siva and conch Samudraghosham of lord Siva was also sported by Aswattama.
[Contains English characters] It is also true that several Pallava princes who took charges in Kanchi came from many distant islands also where extended the authority of the great kings, let alone from Indian subcontinent.
[Contains English characters] The rule of the Pallavas apparently starts as early as 275 CE, but their greatest epoch corresponds to the 7th and 8th century.
[Contains English characters] The history of the early Pallavas has not yet been satisfactorily settled.
[Contains English characters] The earliest documentation on the Pallavas is the three copper-plate grants, belonging to Skandavarman I and written in Prakrit.
[Contains English characters] Skandavarman appears to have been the first great ruler of the early Pallavas, though there are references to other early Pallavas who were probably predecessors of Skandavarman.
[Contains English characters] Skandavarman extended his dominions from the Krishna in the north to the Pennar in the south and to the Bellary district in the West.
[Contains English characters] He performed the Aswamedha and other Vedic sacrifices and bore the शीर्षक of Supreme King of Kings devoted to dharma.
[Contains English characters] In the reign of Simhavarman IV, who ascended the throne in 436 BC, the fallen prestige of the Pallavas was restored.
[Contains English characters] He recovered the territories lost to the Vishnukundins in the north up to the mouth of the Krishna.
[Contains English characters] The early Pallava history from this period onwards is furnished by a dozen or so copper-plate grants in Sanskrit.
[Contains English characters] They are all dated in the regnal years of the kings.
[Contains English characters] With the accession of Nandivarman I, the decline of the early Pallava family was seen.
[Contains English characters] The Kadambas had their aggressions and attacked even the headquarters of the Pallavas with the Pallavas taking retaliatory measures by expelling and invading Kadamba territories in Karnataka.
[Contains English characters] In coastal Andhra the Vishnukundins established their ascendency.
[Contains English characters] The Pallava authority was confined to Tondaimandalam.
[Contains English characters] With the accession of Simhavishnu, father of Mahendravarman I, c.
[Contains English characters] 575 BC, the Pallava revival began in the south.
[Contains English characters] The incursion of the Kalabhras and the confusion in the Tamil country was broken by the Pandya Kadungon and the Pallava Simhavishnu.
[Contains English characters] The Pallava kingdom began to gain both in territory and influence over the South Indian peninsula and were a regional power by the end of the 6th century.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas exercised control over their southern neighbours of Cholas and Pandyas.
[Contains English characters] But their history is marked by the continuous conflict with the Badami Chalukyas.
[Contains English characters] Narasimhavarma I and Paramesvaravarma I were the kings who stand out with glorious achievements in both military and architectural spheres.
[Contains English characters] Nandivarma II built the Shore Temple.
[Contains English characters] During the thirteenth and the fourteenth centuries CE, a small principality of the Kadava dynasty came into brief prominence.
[Contains English characters] These rulers claimed descent from the Pallavas.
[Contains English characters] The notable rulers of this dynasty are Kopperunchinga I, and his son and successor Kopperunchinga II .
[Contains English characters] Together they extended the influence of their kingdom and played a major part in the ultimate demise of the Chola dynasty.
[Contains English characters] Pallavas were followers of Hinduism and made gifts of land to gods and brahmins.
[Contains English characters] In line with the prevalent customs, some of the rulers performed the Aswamedha and other Vedic sacrifices.
[Contains English characters] They were, however, tolerant of other faiths.
[Contains English characters] The Chinese monk Xuanzang who visited Kanchipuram during the reign of Narasimhavarman I reported that there were 100 Buddhist monasteries, and 80 temples in Kanchipuram.
[Contains English characters] Mahendravarman I was initially a patron of the जैन धर्म faith.
[Contains English characters] He later re-converted to Hinduism under the influence of the Saiva saint Appar with the revival of Hinduism during the Bhakti movement in South India.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas were instrumental in the transition from rock-cut architecture to stone temples.
[Contains English characters] The earliest examples of Pallava constructions are rock-cut temples dating from 610–690 CE and structural temples between 690–900 CE.
[Contains English characters] A number of rock-cut cave temples bear the inscription of the Pallava king, Mahendravarman I and his successors.
[Contains English characters] The greatest accomplishments of the Pallava architecture are the rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram.
[Contains English characters] There are excavated pillared halls and monolithic shrines known as rathas in Mahabalipuram.
[Contains English characters] Early temples were mostly dedicated to Shiva.
[Contains English characters] The Kailasanatha temple in Kanchipuram and the Shore Temple built by Narasimhavarman II are fine examples of the Pallava style temples.

[Contains English characters] In the classic discipline of rhetoric, parrhesia is a figure of speech described as: to speak candidly or to ask forgiveness for so speaking.
[Contains English characters] The term is borrowed from the Greek παρρησία meaning literally to speak everything and by extension to speak freely, to speak boldly, or boldness.
[Contains English characters] It implies not only freedom of speech, but the obligation to speak the truth for the common good, even at personal risk.
[Contains English characters] Parrhesia was a fundamental component of the democracy of Classical Athens.
[Contains English characters] In assemblies and the courts Athenians were free to say almost anything, and in the theatre, playwrights such as Aristophanes made full use of the right to ridicule whomever they chose.
[Contains English characters] Elsewhere there were limits to what might be said; freedom to discuss politics, morals, religion, or to criticize people would depend on context: by whom it was made, and when, and how, and where.
[Contains English characters] If a man was seen as immoral, or his views went contrary to popular opinion, then there were great risks involved in making use of such an unbridled freedom of speech, as Socrates found out when he was sentenced to death for introducing new gods and corrupting the young.
[Contains English characters] Parrhesia was also a central concept for the Cynic philosophers, as epitomized in the shameless speech of Diogenes of Sinope.
[Contains English characters] A related use of parrhesia is found in the Greek New Testament, where it means bold speech, the ability of believers to hold their own in discourse before political and religious authorities .
[Contains English characters] It is also used to describe the reply Jesus made to the Pharisees .
[Contains English characters] See Heinrich Schlier, παρρησία, παρρησιάζομαι, Theological Dictionary of the New Testament, Gerhard Kittel and Gerhard Friedrich, Eds.

[Contains English characters] V, pp. 871ff. Michel Foucault developed the concept of parrhesia as a mode of discourse in which one speaks openly and truthfully about ones opinions and ideas without the use of rhetoric, manipulation, or generalization .
[Contains English characters] Foucaults use of parrhesia, he tells us, is troubled by our modern day Cartesian model of evidential necessity.
[Contains English characters] For Descartes, truth is the same as the undeniable.
[Contains English characters] Whatever can be doubted must be, and, thus, speech that is not examined or criticized does not necessarily have a valid relation to truth.
[Contains English characters] There are several conditions upon which the traditional Ancient Greek notion of parrhesia relies.
[Contains English characters] One who uses parrhesia is only recognized as doing so if he holds a credible relationship to the truth, if he serves as critic to either himself or popular opinion or culture, if the revelation of this truth places him in a position of danger and he persists in speaking the truth, nevertheless, as he feels it is his moral, social, and/or political obligation.
[Contains English characters] Further, a user of parrhesia must be in a social position less empowered than those to whom he is revealing.
[Contains English characters] For instance, a pupil speaking the truth to an instructor would be an accurate example of parrhesia, whereas an instructor revealing the truth to his or her pupils would not.
[Contains English characters] Foucault sums up the Ancient Greek concept of parrhesia as such: So you see, the parrhesiastes is someone who takes a risk.
[Contains English characters] Of course, this risk is not always a risk of life.
[Contains English characters] When, for example, you see a friend doing something wrong and you risk incurring his anger by telling him he is wrong, you are acting as a parrhesiastes.
[Contains English characters] In such a case, you do not risk your life, but you may hurt him by your remarks, and your friendship may consequently suffer for it.
[Contains English characters] If, in a political debate, an orator risks losing his popularity because his opinions are contrary to the majoritys opinion, or his opinions may usher in a political scandal, he uses parrhesia.
[Contains English characters] Parrhesia, then, is linked to courage in the face of danger: it demands the courage to speak the truth in spite of some danger.
[Contains English characters] And in its extreme form, telling the truth takes place in the game of life or death.
[Contains English characters] and To summarize the foregoing, parrhesia is a kind of verbal activity where the speaker has a specific relation to truth through frankness, a certain relationship to his own life through danger, a certain type of relation to himself or other people through criticism, and a specific relation to moral law through freedom and duty.
[Contains English characters] More precisely, parrhesia is a verbal activity in which a speaker expresses his personal relationship to truth, and risks his life because he recognizes truth-telling as a duty to improve or help other people .
[Contains English characters] In parrhesia, the speaker uses his freedom and chooses frankness instead of persuasion, truth instead of falsehood or silence, the risk of death instead of life and security, criticism instead of flattery, and moral duty instead of self-interest and moral apathy.
[Contains English characters] ParrhesiaThe term was described by Michel Foucault used to the concept of discourse in which one speaks openly and truthful about his own opinions and his ideas without using rhetorical elements, manipulative speech or generalizations.
[Contains English characters] Foucaults Verwendung von Parrhesia wird durch unsere modernen cartesianischen Modelle des Beweiszwanges getrübt.
[Contains English characters] Foucaults use of Parrhesia is clouded by our modern Cartesian models of evidence coercion.
[Contains English characters] Für Descartes ist Wahrheit dasselbe wie das, was unleugbar ist.
[Contains English characters] For Descartes, truth is the same as that which is undeniable.
[Contains English characters] Wenn es Zweifel geben kann, muss es Zweifel geben.
[Contains English characters] While there may be doubts, there must be doubts.
[Contains English characters] Daher ist die Rede, die nicht genau untersucht oder kritisiert wird, nicht notwendigerweise in eine Beziehung zur Wahrheit zu setzen.
[Contains English characters] Therefore, the question that is not scrutinized or criticized not necessarily share a relationship with the truth.
[Contains English characters] Es gibt mehrere Bedingungen für die traditionelle altgriechische Idee von Parrhesia .
[Contains English characters] There are several conditions for the traditional ancient Greek idea of Parrhesia.
[Contains English characters] Einer, der Parrhesia verwendet, wird nur als solcher erkannt, wenn er eine glaubwürdige Beziehung zur Wahrheit hat, wenn er sich selber oder populäre Meinungen der Kultur kritisiert, wenn die Offenbarung dieser Wahrheit ihn in Gefahr bringt, und er dennoch die Wahrheit spricht, weil er es als seine moralische, soziale und/oder politische Pflicht erachtet, dies zu tun.
[Contains English characters] One that uses Parrhesia, is only recognized as such if he has a credible relationship with the truth when he himself, or popular views of culture criticism when the revelation of this truth brings him into danger, and yet he speaks the truth, because he considered as his moral, social and / or political obligation to do so.
[Contains English characters] Weiterhin muss eine Parrhesia -sprechende Person in einer sozialen Position sein, die unterhalb derjenigen ist, die sie kritisiert.
[Contains English characters] Furthermore, his must be a Parrhesia-speaking person in a social position which is below that which they criticized.
[Contains English characters] Beispielsweise ein Schüler, der die Wahrheit seiner Lehrerin gegenüber ausspricht, wäre ein zutreffendes Beispiel von Parrhesia ; ein Lehrer jedoch, der die Wahrheit seiner Schülerin mitteilt, ist dies nicht.
[Contains English characters] For example, a student who speaks the truth to his teacher, would be a true example of Parrhesia, a teacher, however, that tells the truth of his pupil, this is not.

[Contains English characters] Victory is a term, originally in applied to warfare, given to success achieved in personal combat, after military operations in general or, by extension, in any competition.
[Contains English characters] Success in a military campaign is considered a strategic victory, while the success in a military engagement is a tactical victory.
[Contains English characters] In terms of human emotion, victory is accompanied with strong feelings of elation, and in human behaviour is often accompanied with movements and poses paralleling threat display preceding the combat, associated with the excess endorphin built up preceding and during combat.
[Contains English characters] Victory dances and victory cries similarly parallel war dances and war cries performed before the outbreak of physical violence.
[Contains English characters] Examples of victory behaviour reported in Roman antiquity, where the term originates, are the victory songs of the Batavi mercenaries serving under Gaius Julius Civilis after the victory over Quintus Petillius Cerialis in the Batavian rebellion of 69, and also the abominable song to Wodan, sung by the Langobards at their victory celebration in 579. The sacrificial animal was a goat, around whose head the Langobard danced in a circle while singing their victory hymn .
[Contains English characters] In the Roman Republic, victories were celebrated by triumph ceremonies and monuments such as victory columns .
[Contains English characters] A trophy is a token of victory taken from the defeated party, such as the enemys weapons, or body parts .
[Contains English characters] In mythology, victory is often deified, as in Greek Nike or Roman Victoria.
[Contains English characters] Archetypical victories of good over evil, or of light over dark etc.
[Contains English characters] are a recurring theme in mythology and fairy tales.
[Contains English characters] The victorious agent is a hero, often portrayed as engaging in hand-to-hand combat with a monster .
[Contains English characters] Sol invictus of Roman mythology became an epithet of Christ in Christian mythology.
[Contains English characters] The resurrection of Christ is presented as a victory over Death and Sin by Paul of Tarsus .
[Contains English characters] Latinate victory from the 14th century replaces Old English sige, a frequent element in Germanic names, cognate to Celtic sego- and Sanskrit sahas.

The first Tamil newspaper, Swadesamitran, was launched in 1899.
