[Contains English characters] Lizards are a widespread group of squamate reptiles, with approximately 6,000 species, ranging across all continents except Antarctica, as well as most oceanic island chains.
[Contains English characters] The group, traditionally recognized as the suborder Lacertilia, is defined as all extant members of the Lepidosauria that are neither sphenodonts nor snakes – they form an evolutionary grade.
[Contains English characters] While the snakes are recognized as falling phylogenetically within the Toxicofera clade from which they evolved, the sphenodonts are the sister group to the squamates, the larger monophyletic group, which includes both the lizards and the snakes.
[Contains English characters] Lizards typically have feet and external ears, while snakes lack both of these characteristics.
[Contains English characters] However, because they are defined negatively as excluding snakes, lizards have no unique distinguishing characteristic as a group.
[Contains English characters] Lizards and snakes share a movable quadrate bone, distinguishing them from the sphenodonts, which have more primitive and solid diapsid skulls.
[Contains English characters] Many lizards can detach their tails to escape from predators, an act called autotomy.
[Contains English characters] Vision, including color vision, is particularly well developed in most lizards, and most communicate with body language or bright colors on their bodies, as well as with pheromones.
[Contains English characters] Lizards are the most speciose among extant reptiles, comprising about 60% of all living species.
[Contains English characters] The adult length of species within the suborder ranges from a few centimeters for chameleons such as Brookesia micra and geckos such as Sphaerodactylus ariasae to nearly 3 m in the case of the largest living varanid lizard, the Komodo dragon.
[Contains English characters] Some extinct varanids reached great size.
[Contains English characters] The extinct aquatic mosasaurs reached 17 m, and the giant monitor Megalania is estimated to have reached perhaps 7 m .
[Contains English characters] The name Sauria was coined by James Macartney ; it was the Latinisation of the French name Sauriens, coined by Alexandre Brongniart for an order of reptiles in the classification proposed by the author, containing lizards and crocodilians, later discovered not to be each others closest relatives.
[Contains English characters] Later authors used the term Sauria in a more restricted sense, i. e. as a synonym of Lacertilia, a suborder of Squamata that includes all lizards but excludes snakes.
[Contains English characters] This classification is rarely used today because Sauria so-defined is a paraphyletic group.
[Contains English characters] It was defined as a clade by Jacques Gauthier, Arnold G.
[Contains English characters] Kluge and Timothy Rowe as the group containing the most recent common ancestor of archosaurs and lepidosaurs and all its descendants.
[Contains English characters] A different definition was formulated by Michael deBraga and Olivier Rieppel who defined Sauria as the clade containing the most recent common ancestor of Choristodera, Archosauromorpha and Lepidosauromorpha and all their descendants.
[Contains English characters] However, neither of these uses have not gained wide acceptance among researchers specializing in lizards.

[Contains English characters] साचा:H:h Metawikipedia:Help:Advanced templates येथील पानाचे भाषांतर या पानात ,प्रगत साचांचे तंत्रज्ञान नमुद केले आहे,विशेषतः,साच्यांच्या बदलणार्‍या नावांचा वापर तसेच साच्यांच्या कार्यकक्षांची नावे इत्यादी.
[Contains English characters] यातील काही खाली नमुद केलेली तंत्रे ही मर्यादित स्वरुपाची असु शकतात तर काही अद्ययावत् नसु शकतात ;उदाहरणार्थ: येथील चर्चा केलेली काही branching techniques यापेक्षा पार्सर क्रिया या जास्त सुटसुटीत असु शकतात. . This page covers advanced template techniques, in particular the use of variable template names and parameter names in templates.
[Contains English characters] Readers should be thoroughly familiar with the standard template techniques found in Help:Template.
[Contains English characters] Some techniques described below may be outdated or of limited use; for example, ParserFunctions may be more convenient than some of the branching techniques discussed.
[Contains English characters] सर्वसाधारणपणे,ही तंत्रे पुनर्कृति recursive पद्धतीच्या साच्यांवर प्रक्रिया करण्यावर अवलंबुन असतात.
[Contains English characters] जेंव्हा एखाद्या साच्यावर प्रक्रिया करण्यात येते,ती साच्याचा संकेतास string values भाषांतरीत करते.
[Contains English characters] दोन महिरपी कंसात text strings बद्ध केल्यावर साच्यांची नावे किंवा बदल नावे म्हणुनही त्यावर पुनर्प्रक्रिया केल्या जाउ शकते.
[Contains English characters] त्याने, string च्या किंमती बदलल्यामुळे, वेगवेगळे निकाल मिळतात.
[Contains English characters] In general, these techniques rely on the recursive processing of templates.
[Contains English characters] When a template is processed, it translates template code into string values.
[Contains English characters] These are often sent directly to the web browser for display, but they can be treated as code themselves.
[Contains English characters] By enclosing the text strings in double-curly-brackets, for instance, they can be reprocessed as template names or variable names, producing different results as the string values are changed.
[Contains English characters] In some cases, it may be useful for a template to call different templates depending on a variable or a passed parameter.
[Contains English characters] This allows a type of branching that can be simpler than Parser functions, though they are generally less versatile.
[Contains English characters] उदाहरण: The extra spaces in the above examples are needed: without them, the code is not processed as a template or a magic word, but just as a plain text string like so: NAMESPACE.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Hist5 Since there is no convenient way to test substring values, these techniques work best if the variable template has only a limited number of possible values.
[Contains English characters] For example, the variable CURRENTDAYNAME has only seven possible values, so all cases can be handled with seven templates, and the variable NAMESPACE currently has 18 possible values.
[Contains English characters] On the other hand, CURRENTTIME has 1440 possible values, which would require the creation of 1440 template pages or redirects, which would be impractical.
[Contains English characters] Even with parser functions, all 1440 values would have to be listed and m:Template:minute .
[Contains English characters] In cases like that, it would be better to construct the template with multiple parameters that each only take a few values, rather than trying to account for all possibilities in a single parameter.
[Contains English characters] If a template depends on PAGENAME, then the many possible values of PAGENAME may not be a problem.
[Contains English characters] Only the pagenames of the pages that call the template apply, and these can be limited to a small, enumerable set.
[Contains English characters] Templates can be passed as parameters to other templates.
[Contains English characters] This can mean either that the template is evaluated and the result is passed as a parameter or that the template name is passed and evaluated as part of the other template.
[Contains English characters] A parameter name in a template can be a variable.
[Contains English characters] This is useful if you want the behavior of a template to change based on the information that is provided to it.
[Contains English characters] Choosing parameters contextually - t pnd|parameter name Template:t p contains capital is the capital of country, with two parameters - capital and country.
[Contains English characters] साचा:Timc can be used to select which parameter is used in a particular case.
[Contains English characters] Thus: This applies to integer parameters as well, since integer parameters can be specified using the #= notation.
[Contains English characters] Passing the integer value N to t pnd as its parameter will make it look for the Nth unnamed parameter.
[Contains English characters] The following branching methods are generally obsolete; Parser Functions give easier forms of control.
[Contains English characters] However, they may be useful in particular situations, and point out some unintuitive features of template behavior.
[Contains English characters] Variables names can also be generated as variables.
[Contains English characters] | ns:0=gallery| ns:2=user page| ns:4=project page| ns:6=media file| ns:8=system message| ns:10=template| ns:14=category| TALKSPACE=talk page| pagedocumentation , the last use of the parameter evaluates to a number #, and the entire phrase ns:# is evaluated as a template.
[Contains English characters] Thus, namespace|4 gives gallery, where Meta is the name of Namespace 4. साचा:H:f

[Contains English characters] साचा:Mergefromसाचा:Cuisine of India The cuisine of Kerala is linked in all its richness to the history, geography, demography and culture of the land.
[Contains English characters] Since many of Keralas Hindus are vegetarian by religion, and because Kerala has large minorities of Muslims and Christians that are predominantly non-vegetarians, Kerala cuisine has a multitude of both vegetarian and dishes prepared using fish, poultry and meat.
[Contains English characters] For over 2000 years, Kerala has been visited by ocean-goers, including traders from Greece, Rome, the eastern Mediterranean, Arab countries, and युरोप .
[Contains English characters] Thus, Kerala cuisine is a blend of indigenous dishes and foreign dishes adapted to Kerala tastes.
[Contains English characters] Coconuts grow in abundance in Kerala, and consequently, grated coconut and coconut milk are widely used in dishes and curries as a thickener and flavouring ingredient.
[Contains English characters] Keralas long coastline, numerous rivers and backwater networks, and strong fishing industry have contributed to many sea- and river-food based dishes.
[Contains English characters] Rice is grown in abundance, and could be said, along with tapioca, to be the main starch ingredient used in Kerala food.
[Contains English characters] Having been a major production area of spices for thousands of years, black pepper, cardamom, cloves, ginger, and cinnamon play a large part in its food.
[Contains English characters] Pre-independence Kerala was split into the princely states of Travancore and Kochi in the south, and the Malabar district in the north; the erstwhile split is reflected in the recipes and cooking style of each area.
[Contains English characters] Both Travancore and Malabar cuisine consists of a variety of vegetarian dishes using many vegetables and fruits that are not commonly used in curries elsewhere in India including plantains, bitter gourd, taro, Colocasia, Ash gourd, etc.
[Contains English characters] However, their style of preparation and names of the prepares dishes may vary.
[Contains English characters] Malabar has an array of vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes such as pathiri, porotta, and the kerala variant of the popular biriyani, probably from Arab lands.
[Contains English characters] Central Travancore region boasts of a parade of dishes that is largely identified with the Christians of the region.
[Contains English characters] In addition to historical diversity, the cultural influences, particularly the large percentages of Muslims and Syrian Christians have also contributed unique dishes and styles to Kerala cuisine, especially non-vegetarian dishes.
[Contains English characters] The meat eating habit of the people have been historically limited by religious taboos.
[Contains English characters] Brahmins eschew non vegetarian items and Hindus historically do not eat beef.
[Contains English characters] However, most of modern day Hindus do not observe any dietary taboos, except a few of those belonging to upper caste .
[Contains English characters] Muslims do not eat pork and other items forbidden by Islamic law.
[Contains English characters] Historically, Kerala had been a part of the Tamil-speaking area, and Tamilian influence is seen in the popularity of sambar, idli and dosa.
[Contains English characters] European influence is reflected in the numerous bakeries selling cakes, cream horns, and Western-style yeast-leavened bread, and in Anglo-Indian cuisine.
[Contains English characters] The import of potatoes, tomatoes, and chili peppers from the Americas led to their enthusiastic use in Kerala, although except for the ubiquitous peppers, the other ingredients are used more sparingly.
[Contains English characters] As with almost all Indian food, spices play an important part in Kerala cuisine.
[Contains English characters] The main spices used are cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, green and red peppers, cloves, garlic, cumin seeds, coriander, turmeric, and so on.
[Contains English characters] Few fresh herbs are used, unlike in European cuisine, and mainly consist of the commonly used curry leaf, and the occasional use of fresh coriander and mint.
[Contains English characters] Tamarind, kodampuli, and lime are used to make sauces sour, as sour sauces are very popular in Kerala.
[Contains English characters] Sweet and sour dishes are however, rare, but exceptions like the ripe mango version of the pulissery and tamarind-jaggery-ginger chutney known as puliinji or injipuli are popular.
[Contains English characters] Kerala cuisine offers many delicious vegetarian breakfast dishes that are often relatively unknown outside the state.
[Contains English characters] These include Puttu and kadala, idli, sambar, dosa and chutney, pidiyan, Idiyappam, Paal-Appam, a circular, fluffy, crisp-edged pancake made of rice flour fermented with a small amount of toddy or wine, etc.
[Contains English characters] Idiyapam and Paalappam are accompanied by mutton, chicken or vegetable stew or a curry of beef or fish moli .
[Contains English characters] The staple food of Kerala, like most South-Indian states, is rice.
[Contains English characters] Unlike other states, however, many people in Kerala prefer parboiled rice .
[Contains English characters] Kanji, a kind of rice porridge, is also popular.
[Contains English characters] Tapioca, called kappa in Kerala, is popular in central Kerala and in the highlands, and is frequently eaten with fish curry.
[Contains English characters] Rice is usually consumed with one or more curries.
[Contains English characters] Accompaniments with rice may include upperis, rasam, chips, and/or buttermilk .
[Contains English characters] Vegetarian dinners usually consist of multiple courses, each involving rice, one main dish, and one or more side-dishes.
[Contains English characters] Kerala cooking uses coconut oil almost exclusively, although health concerns and cost have led to coconut oil being replaced to some extent by palm oil and vegetable oil.
[Contains English characters] Popular vegetarian dishes include sambar, aviyal, Kaalan, theeyal, thoran, pulisherry, olan, erisherry, puliinji, payaru, kappa, etc.
[Contains English characters] Vegetarian dishes often consist of fresh spices that are liquefied and crushed to make a paste-like texture to dampen rice.
[Contains English characters] Common non-vegetarian dishes include stew, traditional or chicken curry, chicken fry, fish/chicken/mutton molly, fish curry, fish fry, lobster fry, Spicy Beef Fry, Spicy Steamed Fish etc.
[Contains English characters] Biriyani, a Mughal dish consists of rice cooked along with meat, onions, chillies and other spices.
[Contains English characters] Although rice and tapioca may be considered the original Kerala starch staples, wheat, in the form of chappatis or parathas, is now very commonly eaten, especially at dinner time.
[Contains English characters] Numerous little streetside vendors offer an oily parathas with meat, egg, or vegetable curry for dinner.
[Contains English characters] Grains such as ragi and millet, although common in the arid parts of South India, have not gained a foothold in Kerala.
[Contains English characters] Kerala is known for its traditional banquet or sadhya, a vegetarian meal served with boiled rice and a host of side-dishes served especially during special occasions and festivals.
[Contains English characters] The sadhya is complemented by payasam, a sweet dessert native to Kerala.
[Contains English characters] The sadhya is, as per custom, served on a banana leaf, and is a formal-style meal with three or more courses of rice with a side-dish .
[Contains English characters] In south Kerala the Payasam in followed by more .
[Contains English characters] Whereas in North Kerala it is considered to be the last dish to be served.
[Contains English characters] A typical sadhya would have Due to limited influence of Arab & Central Asian food on Kerala, the use of sweets is not as widespread as in North India.
[Contains English characters] Kerala does not have any indigenous cold desserts, but hot/warm desserts are popular.
[Contains English characters] The most popular example is undoubtedly the payasam: a preparation of milk, coconut extract, sugar, cashews, dry grapes, etc.
[Contains English characters] Payasam can be made with many base constituents, including Paal payasam, Ada payasam, Paripu payasam, Pazham pradhamam, Gothambu payasam etc.
[Contains English characters] Ada payasam is especially popular during the festival of Onam.
[Contains English characters] Most payasams can also be consumed chilled.
[Contains English characters] Jaggery or molasses is a common sweetening ingredient, although white sugar is gaining ground.
[Contains English characters] Fruit, especially the small yellow bananas, are often eaten after a meal or at any time of the day.
[Contains English characters] Plantains, uncooked or steamed, are popularly eaten for breakfast or tea.
[Contains English characters] Other popular sweets include Unniappam, pazham-pori, and kozhukkatta .
[Contains English characters] Cakes, ice-creams, cookies and puddings are equally common.
[Contains English characters] Generally, except for payasam, most sweets are not eaten as dessert but as a tea-time snack.
[Contains English characters] Kerala cuisine also has a variety of pickles and chutneys, and crunchy pappadums, banana chips, jackfruit chips, kozhalappam, achappam, cheeda, and churuttu.
[Contains English characters] Being mostly a hot and humid area, Keralites have developed a variety of drinks to cope with thirst.
[Contains English characters] A variety of what might be called herbal teas are served during mealtimes.
[Contains English characters] Cumin seeds, ginger or coriander seeds are boiled in water and served warm or at room temperature.
[Contains English characters] In addition to the improved taste, the spices also have digestive and other medicinal properties.
[Contains English characters] Sambharam, a diluted buttermilk often flavoured with ginger, lime leaves, green chili peppers etc.
[Contains English characters] was very commonly drunk, although it has been replaced to some extent by soda pop.
[Contains English characters] Coffee and tea drunk black, or with milk and white sugar or unrefined palm sugar, are commonly drunk.
[Contains English characters] Numerous small shops dotted around the land sell fresh lime juice, and many now offer milk shakes and other fruit juices.
[Contains English characters] There are utensils that are used in Kerala which are significant to cuisine in Kerala.
[Contains English characters] An aduppu is a square hearth, Mun Chatti is cooking pot made from clay, Cheena Chatti is a deep frying pan.
[Contains English characters] Food is extremely important when it comes to rituals or festivals.
[Contains English characters] Food offerings in ritual are important in Kerala and throughout South India.
[Contains English characters] Food offerings are often related to the gods of religions.
[Contains English characters] In India, there are numerous offerings for Hindu gods and there are many differences between food offerings in North and South India.
[Contains English characters] Most offerings contain more than one type of food.
[Contains English characters] There are many reasons why people use the practice of food offerings.
[Contains English characters] Some are to express love, or negotiate or thank gods.
[Contains English characters] It can also be used to stress certain structural features of Hinduism.
[Contains English characters] Of course, not every ritual’s gods require food offerings.
[Contains English characters] Most have a liking for certain foods.
[Contains English characters] For example, butter is one of the preferred foods by the god Krishna.
[Contains English characters] Also, wild orange and a sugarcane stalk are related to Ganapati.
[Contains English characters] There is a division of the Hindu pantheon into pure and impure deities which is stressed, but shaped by food offerings.
[Contains English characters] Pure deities are offered vegetarian foods while impure deities are offered meat due to their craving for blood.
[Contains English characters] A specific dish is offered to both pure and impure deities.
[Contains English characters] That is a flour lamp which is made of sweetened rice-flour paste which is scooped out and packed with ghee.
[Contains English characters] The flour lamp is only partially baked and then eaten.
[Contains English characters] Another aspect of food offerings is the hierarchy that foods have.
[Contains English characters] It may seem strange that there is a hierarchy for foods, but it is because there is a dual opposition between the pure and impure deities which is hierarchal.
[Contains English characters] There are two gods which have this dual opposition.
[Contains English characters] They are Vishnu and Siva.
[Contains English characters] Ferro-Luzzi explains that Vishnu is viewed as kind while the offerings that are given to Siva are more frugal.
[Contains English characters] An offering to Siva might be likely to be plain rice with no salt or other toppings, while an offering to Vishnu may resemble a South Indian dish which can consist of rice with other side dishes.
[Contains English characters] Specifically in South Indian offerings, they are offered in numbers.
[Contains English characters] For example, the number three is important in Kerala offerings.
[Contains English characters] There are the trimadhura which translates into the three sweets.
[Contains English characters] All of these practices of food offerings in ritual are important in Kerala culture as well as South Indian culture.
[Contains English characters] The last decade has seen the rise of cooking as sacred ritual in South Kerala, almost exclusively by women.
[Contains English characters] This practice, called Pongala, seems to have been historically associated with the Attukal Temple in Trivandrum city.
[Contains English characters] According to the Guinness Book of Records, Attukal Pongala is the largest gathering of women in the world.
[Contains English characters] Women participants of the pongala come equipped with cooking pots, dry fuel and ingredients such as rice flour, palm sugar and condiments, often the previous evening, and set up their hearths around the temple on the morning of the day of the festival.
[Contains English characters] Often, the women take over most of the roads and lanes of Trivandrum city during the pongala day.
[Contains English characters] In 2009, the estimated number of women who participated was 2.5 million.
[Contains English characters] The women wait until the Attukal temple ceremoniously distributes the fire, and set about their cooking when the fire reaches them, passed from hearth to hearth.
[Contains English characters] They go home with the cooked offerings by late afternoon.
[Contains English characters] While males are not allowed in the area, they help out my providing support to arriving and departing women by organizing transportation, and distributing free beverages.
[Contains English characters] Trivandrum city, police and civil authorities have been successfully able to manage the festival, but it is quintessentially a womens festival.
[Contains English characters] Despite the lack of amenities, the considerable hardship involved in transportation of cooking equipment and ingredients, and the blazing February sun, the numbers of participants seem to be rising year after year, and include some of the well-known faces from cinema, social circles as well as commoners.
[Contains English characters] It is also observed that the practice of pongala is rapidly spreading to many other temples in Trivandrum city and district.

[Contains English characters] साचा:Tocleft WPBannerMeta is a meta-template, which can be used to create WikiProject banners, enabling new projects to easily create a banner to place on article talk pages, ensuring standardisation between projects.
[Contains English characters] A list of all WikiProject banners using this meta-template can be found at What links here: WPBannerMeta WPBannerMeta can be used at varying levels of complexity, from the very simple to the extremely complicated.
[Contains English characters] Simple options are listed here first, with complexity increasing down the page.
[Contains English characters] WPBannerMeta takes two different types of parameters, formatting and display.
[Contains English characters] The formatting parameters customise the meta-template for a particular project, defining link targets, categories, images and text.
[Contains English characters] All formatting parameters use UPPERCASE and underscores, instead of spaces .
[Contains English characters] Display parameters customise the template output for each individual article that the banner is displayed on.
[Contains English characters] These are the parameters which are entered on the talk page and they must be passed through the project banner to the meta-template underneath.
[Contains English characters] To pass the parameter foo, you need to include the code foo=foo|.
[Contains English characters] In the examples below, a WikiProject banner will be constructed for the nonexistent WikiProject Tulips.
[Contains English characters] #assessment:Tulips||Unknown Many projects use the Version 1.0 Assessment schema to grade their articles by quality and the corresponding importance scale to place their articles in order of priority.
[Contains English characters] In order to implement WP:1.0, which uses a bot to automatically compile its statistics tables, you will need to follow the instructions at /Using the bot, as well as those outlined here.
[Contains English characters] #assessment:Tulips|GA|Top Built into WPBannerMeta is the ability to display a number of other fields that contain useful information about the article or task-forces to which it is affiliated.
[Contains English characters] There is also a predefined attention field to flag articles in need of immediate attention and a needs-infobox field for flagging articles in need of an infobox.
[Contains English characters] #assessment:Tulips|C|Unknown WPBannerMeta can accommodate up to five task forces, each with its own image, links and importance scale, if desired.
[Contains English characters] The following parameters are available: WPBannerMeta incorporates a number of hooks where advanced or customised features can be added.
[Contains English characters] These should take the form of a subtemplate passed to the relevant hook parameter.
[Contains English characters] Any relevant parameters should then be passed to the hook template – it may be necessary to repeat parameters that are already passed to the main template .
[Contains English characters] If you write a hook that you think other projects could use, please copy or move it to a subpage of Template:WPBannerMeta/hooks and add it to the list on that page.
[Contains English characters] WPBannerMeta uses a mask to normalise the values given to the |class= parameter, to ensure that invalid inputs are discarded and that equivalent inputs appear the same .
[Contains English characters] This mask effectivley controls which extended assessment scale values are accepted by the template .
[Contains English characters] Projects which want to use more obscure assessment classes or to not use all of the standard classes can define their own custom mask, which will override WPBannerMetas default.
[Contains English characters] This meta-template automatically categorises all instances into Category:WikiProject banners.
[Contains English characters] It is not necessary to include a category link in the documentation for each project banner.
[Contains English characters] Normal project banners, which are substituted rather than transcluded, usually show up in Category:WikiProject banners, allowing for a periodic cleanout.
[Contains English characters] Banners using WPBannerMeta do not appear in this category when substituted, making it easier for them to get lost.

[Contains English characters] The carved and painted wood casing represents a tiger savaging a near life-size European man.
[Contains English characters] Mechanisms inside the tiger and mans bodies make one hand of the man move, emit a wailing sound from his mouth and grunts from the tiger.
[Contains English characters] In addition a flap on the side of the tiger folds down to reveal the keyboard of a small pipe organ with 18 notes.
[Contains English characters] The tiger was created for Tipu and makes use of his personal emblem of the tiger and expresses his hatred of his enemy, the British of the East India Company.
[Contains English characters] The tiger was discovered in his summer palace after East India Company troops stormed Tipus capital in 1799. The Governor General, Lord Mornington sent the Tiger to Britain initially intending it to be an exhibit in the Tower of London.
[Contains English characters] The tiger was first exhibited to the London public in 1808 in India House, the offices of the East India Company in London.
[Contains English characters] It was later transferred to the Victoria and Albert Museum in 1880 .
[Contains English characters] It now forms part of the permanent exhibit on the Imperial courts of South India.
[Contains English characters] From the moment it arrived in London to the present day, Tipus Tiger has been a popular attraction to the public.
[Contains English characters] Tipus Tiger was originally made for Tipu Sultan in the Kingdom of Mysore around 1795. Tipu Sultan used the tiger systematically as his emblem, employing tiger motifs on his weapons, on the uniforms of his soldiers, and on the decoration of his palaces.
[Contains English characters] His throne rested upon a probably similar life-size wooden tiger, covered in gold; like other valuable treasures it was broken up for the highly organized prize fund shared out between the British army.
[Contains English characters] Tipu had inherited power from his father Hyder Ali, a Muslim soldier who had risen to become dalwai or commander-in-chief under the ruling Hindu Wodeyar dynasty, but from 1760 was in effect the ruler of the kingdom.
[Contains English characters] Hyder, after initially trying to ally with the British against the Marathas, had later become their firm enemy, as they represented the most effective obstacle to his expansion of his kingdom, and Tipu grew up with violently anti-British feelings.
[Contains English characters] The tiger formed part of a specific group of large caricature images commissioned by Tipu showing European, often specifically British, figures being attacked by tigers or elephants, or being executed, tortured and humiliated and attacked in other ways.
[Contains English characters] Many of these were painted by Tipus orders on the external walls of houses in the main streets of Tipus capital, Seringapatam.
[Contains English characters] Tipu was in close co-operation with the French, who were at war with Britain and still had a presence in South India, and some of the French craftsmen who visited Tipus court probably contributed to the internal works of the tiger.
[Contains English characters] The design may have been inspired by the death in 1792 of Hugh Munro, son of General Sir Hector Munro, who had commanded a division during Sir Eyre Cootes victory at the Battle of Porto Novo in 1781 when Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultans father, was defeated with a loss of 10,000 men during the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
[Contains English characters] Hugh Munro, a civilian visiting India, was attacked and killed by a tiger on the 22 December 1792 while hunting with several companions on Saugor Island in the Bay of Bengal .
[Contains English characters] With overall dimensions for the object of 71.2 cm high and 172 cm long, the man at least is close to life-size.
[Contains English characters] The painted wooden shell forming both figures probably draws upon South Indian traditions of Hindu religious sculpture.
[Contains English characters] It is typically about half an inch thick, and now much reinforced on the inside following bomb damage in World War II.
[Contains English characters] There are many openings at the head end, formed to match the pattern of the inner part of the painted tiger stripes, which allow the sounds from the pipes within to be heard better, and the tiger is obviously male.
[Contains English characters] The top part of the tigers body can be lifted off to inspect the mechanics by removing four screws.
[Contains English characters] The construction of the human figure is similar but the wood is much thicker.
[Contains English characters] Examination and analysis by the V&A conservation department has determined that much of the current paint has been restored or overpainted.
[Contains English characters] The human figure is clearly in European costume, but authorities differ as to whether it represents a soldier or civilian; the current text on the V&A website avoids specifying, other than describing the figure as European.
[Contains English characters] The operation of a crank handle powers several different mechanisms inside Tipus Tiger.
[Contains English characters] A set of bellows expels air through a pipe inside the mans throat, with its opening at his mouth.
[Contains English characters] This produces a wailing sound, simulating the cries of distress of the victim.
[Contains English characters] A mechanical link causes the mans left arm to rise and fall.
[Contains English characters] This action alters the pitch of the wail pipe.
[Contains English characters] Another mechanism inside the tigers head expels air through a single pipe with two tones.
[Contains English characters] This produces a regular grunting sound simulating the roar of the tiger.
[Contains English characters] Concealed behind a flap in the tigers flank is the small ivory keyboard of a two-stop pipe organ in the tigers body, allowing tunes to be played.
[Contains English characters] The style of both shell and workings, and analysis of the metal content of the original brass pipes of the organ, indicates that the tiger was of local manufacture.
[Contains English characters] The presence of French artisans and French army engineers within Tipus court has led many historians to suggest there was French input into the mechanism of this automaton.
[Contains English characters] Tipus Tiger was part of the extensive plunder from Tipus palace captured in the fall of Seringapatam, in which Tipu died, on the 4 May 1799, at the culmination of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
[Contains English characters] An aide-de-camp to the Governor General of the East India Company, Richard Wellesley, 1st Marquess Wellesley, wrote a memorandum describing the discovery of the object: The earliest published drawing of Tippoos Tyger was the frontispiece for the book A Review of the Origin, Progress and Result, of the Late Decisive War in Mysore with Notes by James Salmond, published in London in 1800. It preceded the move of the exhibit from India to England and had a separate preface शीर्षकd Description of the Frontispiece which said: The whole of this design is as large as life, and was executed by order of Tippoo Sultaun, who frequently amused himself with a sight of this emblematic triumph of the Khoodadaud, over the English, Sircar.
[Contains English characters] The piece of machinery was found in a room of the palace at Seringapatam appropriated for the reception of musical instruments, and hence called the Rag Mehal.
[Contains English characters] The original wooden figure from which the drawing is taken will be forwarded, by the ships of this season, to the Chairman of the Court of Directors, to be presented to his Majesty.
[Contains English characters] It is imagined that this characteristic emblem of the ferocious animosity of Tippoo Sultaun against the British Nation may not be thought undeserving of a place in the Tower of London.
[Contains English characters] Unlike Tipus throne, which also featured a large tiger, and many other treasures in the palace, the materials of Tipus Tiger had no intrinsic value, which together with its striking iconography is what preserved it and brought it back to England essentially intact.
[Contains English characters] The Governors of the East India Company had at first intended to present the Tiger to the Crown, with a view to it being displayed in the Tower of London, but then decided but to keep it for the Company.
[Contains English characters] After some time in store, during which period the first of many misguided and wholly unjustified endeavours at improving the piece from a musical point of view may have taken place, it was displayed in the reading-room of the East India Company Museum and Library at East India House in Leadenhall Street, London from July 1808. It rapidly became a very popular exhibit, and the crank-handle controlling the wailing and grunting could apparently be freely turned by the public.
[Contains English characters] The French author Gustave Flaubert visited London in 1851 to see the Great Exhibition, writes Julian Barnes, but finding nothing of interest in the Crystal Palace, visited the East India Company Museum where he was greatly enamoured by Tipus Tiger.
[Contains English characters] By 1843 it was reported that The machine or organ . . . is getting much out of repair, and does not altogether realize the expectation of the visitor.
[Contains English characters] Eventually the crank-handle disappeared, to the great relief of students using the reading-room in which the tiger was displayed, and The Athenaeum later reported that When the East India Company was taken over by the Crown in 1858, the tiger was stored in Fife House, Whitehall until 1868, when it moved down the road to the new India Office, which occupied part of the building still used by todays Foreign and Commonwealth Office.
[Contains English characters] In 1874 it was moved to the India Museum in South Kensington, which was in 1879 dissolved, with the collection distributed between other museums; the V&A records the tiger as acquired in 1880. During World War II the tiger was badly damaged by a German bomb which brought down the roof above it, breaking the wooden casing into several hundred pieces, which were carefully pieced together after the war, so that by 1947 it was back on display.
[Contains English characters] In 1955 it was exhibited in New York at the Museum of Modern Art through the summer and spring.
[Contains English characters] Tipus Tiger is a notable example of early musical automata from India, and also for the fact that it was especially constructed for him.
[Contains English characters] In recent times, Tipus Tiger has formed an essential part of museum exhibitions exploring the historical interface between Eastern and Western civilisation, colonialism, ethnic histories and other subjects, one such being held at the Victoria and Albert Museum itself in Autumn 2004 शीर्षकd Encounters:the meeting of Asia and Europe, 1500–1800.
[Contains English characters] In 1995, The Tiger and the Thistle bi-centennial exhibition was held in Scotland on the topic of Tipu Sultan and the Scots.
[Contains English characters] The organ was considered too fragile to travel to Scotland for the exhibition.
[Contains English characters] Instead, a full-sized replica made of fibre glass and painted by Derek Freeborn, was exhibited in its place.
[Contains English characters] The replica itself was also associated with a historic Scottish event having been made in 1986 for The Enterprising Scot exhibition, which was held to commemorate the October 1985 merger of the Royal Scottish Museum and the National Museum of Antiquities of Scotland to form a new entity - the National Museums of Scotland.
[Contains English characters] Today Tipus Tiger is arguably the best-known single work in the Victoria and Albert Museum as far as the general public is concerned.
[Contains English characters] It is a must-see highlight for school-childrens visits to the Victoria and Albert Museum, and functions as an iconic representation of the Museum, replicated in various forms of memorabilia in the Museum shops including postcards, model kits and stuffed toys.
[Contains English characters] Visitors can no longer operate the mechanism since the device is now kept in a glass case.
[Contains English characters] A small model of this toy is exhibited in Tipu Sultans wooden palace in Bangalore.
[Contains English characters] Tipus Tiger has not been the subject of an official repatriation request, presumably due to the ambiguity underlying Tipus image in the eyes of Indians;:181, although Indian billionaire Vijay Mallya recently purchased Tipus sword and other items associated with him which have been brought back to India.
[Contains English characters] Tipu Sultan identified himself with tigers; his personal epithet was The Tiger of Mysore, his soldiers were dressed in tyger jackets, his personal symbol invoked a tigers face through clever use of calligraphy and the tiger motif is visible on his throne, and other objects in his personal possession, including Tipus Tiger.
[Contains English characters] Accordingly, as per Joseph Sramek, for Tipu the tiger striking down the European in the organ represented his symbolic triumph over the British.
[Contains English characters] The British hunted tigers, not just to emulate the Mughals and other local elites in this royal sport, but also as a symbolic defeat of Tipu Sultan and any other ruler who stood in the path of British domination.
[Contains English characters] The tiger motif was used in the Seringapatam medal which was awarded to those who participated in the 1799 campaign, where the British lion was depicted as overcoming a prostrate tiger, the tiger being the dynastic symbol of Tipus line.
[Contains English characters] The Seringapatam medal was issued in gold for the highest dignitaries who were associated with the campaign as well as select officers on general duty, silver for other dignitaries, field officers and other staff officers, in copper-bronze for the NCOs and in tin for the privates.
[Contains English characters] On the reverse it had a frieze of the storming of the fort while the obverse showed, in the words of a nineteenth century tome on medals, the BRITISH LION subduing the TIGER, the emblem of the late Tippoo Sultans government, with the period when it was effected and the following words ASSUD OTTA-UL GHAULIB, signifying the Lion of God is the conqueror, or the conquering Lion of God.
[Contains English characters] In this manner, the iconography of this automaton was adopted and overturned by the British.
[Contains English characters] :12, 149 When Tipus Tiger was displayed in London in the nineteenth century, British viewers of the time characterised the tiger as a trophy and symbolic justification of British colonial rule.
[Contains English characters] Tipus Tiger along with other trophies such as Tipus sword, the throne of Ranjit Singh, Tantya Topes kurta and Nana Sahebs betel-box which was made of brass, were all displayed as memorabilia of the Mutiny.
[Contains English characters] In one interpretation, the display of Tipus Tiger in South Kensington, served to remind the visitor of the noblesse oblige of the British Empire to bring civilisation to the barbaric lands of which Tipu was king.
[Contains English characters] Tipus Tiger is also notable as a literal image of a tiger killing a British Officer, an important symbol in England at the time, and from about 1820 the Death of Munro became one of the scenes in the repertoire of Staffordshire pottery figurines.
[Contains English characters] Tiger-hunting in the British raj, is also considered to represented not just the political subjugation of India, but in addition, the triumph over Indias environment.
[Contains English characters] The iconography persisted and during the rebellion of 1857, Punch ran a political cartoon showing the Indian rebels as a tiger, attacking a victim in an identical pose to Tipus Tiger, being defeated by the British forces shown by the larger figure of a lion.
[Contains English characters] Motives for collection of articles, such as Tipus Tiger, are seen by Kalter as having a social and cultural context.
[Contains English characters] The collection of Western and Indian art by Tipu Sultan is seen as motivated by the need to display his wealth and legitimise his authority over his subjects who were predominantly Hindu and did not share his religion, viz. Islam. In the case of the East India Company, collection of documents, artefacts and objets dart from India helped develop the idea of a subjugated Indian populace in the minds of the British people, the thought being that the possession of such objects of a culture represented understanding of, dominance over and mastery of that culture.
[Contains English characters] Whether made for Tippoo himself or for some other Indian potentate a century and a half earlier, it is difficult to convey a more lively impression of the mingled ferocity and childish want of taste so characteristic of the majority of Asian princes than will be communicated at once by this truly barbarous piece of music.
[Contains English characters] In a detailed study published in 1987 of the tigers musical and noise-making functions, Arthur W. J. G. Ord-Hume concluded that since coming to Britain, the instrument has been ruthlessly reworked, and in doing so much of its original operating principles have been destroyed.
[Contains English characters] There are two ranks of pipes in the organ, each comprising eighteen notes, are nominally of 4ft pitch and are unisons - i. e. corresponding pipes in each register make sounds of the same musical pitch.
[Contains English characters] This is an unusual layout for a pipe organ although while selecting the two stops together results in more sound . . . there is also detectable a slight beat between the the pipes so creating a celeste effect.
[Contains English characters] . . . it is considered likely that as so much work has been done .
[Contains English characters] . . this characteristic may be more an accident of tuning than an intentional feature.
[Contains English characters] The tigers grunt is made by a single pipe in the tigers head and the mans wail by a single pipe emerging at his mouth and connected to separate bellows located in the mans chest, where they can be accessed by unbolting and lifting off the tiger.
[Contains English characters] The grunt operates by cogs gradually raising the weighted grunt-pipe until it reaches a point where it slips down to fall against its fixed lower-board or reservoir, discharging the air to form the grunting sound Today all the sound-making functions rely on the crank-handle to power them, though Ord-Hume believes this was not originally the case.
[Contains English characters] Works on the noise-making functions included those made over several decades by the famous organ-building firm Henry Willis & Sons, and Henry Willis III, who worked on the tiger in the 1950s, contributed an account to a monograph by Mildred Archer of the V&A.
[Contains English characters] Ord-Hume is generally ready to exempt Willis work from his scathing comments on other drastic restorations, which vandalism is assumed to be by unknown earlier organ-builders.
[Contains English characters] There was a detailed account of the sound-making functions in The Penny Magazine in 1835, whose anonymous author evidently understood things mechanical and organs in particular.
[Contains English characters] From this and Ord-Humes own investigations, he concluded that the original operation of the mans wail had been intermitent, with a wail only being produced after every dozen or so grunts from the tiger above, but that at some date after 1835 the mechanism had been altered to make the wail continuous, and that the bellows for the wail had been replaced with smaller and weaker ones, and the operation of the moving arm altered.
[Contains English characters] Puzzling features of the present instrument include the placing of the handle, which when turned is likely to obstruct a player of the keyboard.
[Contains English characters] Ord-Hume, using the 1835 account, concludes that originally the handle only operated the grunt and wail, while the organ was operated by pulling a string or cord to work the original bellows, now replaced.
[Contains English characters] The keyboard, which is largely original, is unique in construction, with square ivory buttons with round lathe-turned tops instead of conventional keys.
[Contains English characters] Though the mechanical functioning of each button is practical and convenient they are spaced such that it is almost impossible to stretch the hand to play an octave.
[Contains English characters] The buttons are marked with small black spots, differently placed but forming no apparent pattern in relation to the notes produced and corresponding to no known system of marking keys.
[Contains English characters] The two stop control knobs for the organ are located, rather confusingly, a little below the tigers testicles.
[Contains English characters] The instrument is now rarely played, but there is a V&A video of a recent performance.
[Contains English characters] Tipus Tiger has provided inspiration to poets, sculptors, artists and others from the nineteenth century to the present day.
[Contains English characters] The poet John Keats saw Tipus Tiger at the museum in Leadenhall Street and worked it into his satirical verse of 1819, The Cap and Bells.
[Contains English characters] In the poem, a soothsayer visits the court of the Emperor Elfinan.
[Contains English characters] He hears a strange noise and thinks the Emperor is snoring.
[Contains English characters] The French poet, Auguste Barbier, described the tiger and its workings and meditated on its meaning in his poem, Le Joujou du Sultan published in 1837. More recently, the American Modernist poet, Marianne Moore wrote in her 1986 poem Tippoos Tiger about the workings of the automaton, though in fact the tail was never movable: Die Seele, a work by painter Jan Balet shows an angel trumpeting over a flower garden while a tiger devours a uniformed French soldier.
[Contains English characters] The Indian painter Maqbool Fida Husain painted Tipus Tiger in his characteristic style in 1986 titling the work as Tipu Sultans Tiger.
[Contains English characters] The sculptor Dhruva Mistry, when a student at the Royal College of Art, adjacent to the Victoria and Albert Museum, frequently passed Tipus Tiger in its glass case and was inspired to make a fibre-glass and plastic sculpture Tipu in 1986. The sculpture Rabbit eating Astronaut by the artist Bill Reid is a humorous homage to the tiger, the rabbit chomping when its tail is cranked round.

[Contains English characters] The Vela is a festival celebrated in the villages of the Palakkad and Thrissur districts in summer, after the harvest.
[Contains English characters] The prominent crop in this area is rice.
[Contains English characters] After the harvest, the fields are empty and dry, and this is the time for the Vela.
[Contains English characters] The Nemmara Vela is celebrated on a grand scale, equalling the famous Trissur Pooram.
[Contains English characters] The festival is believed to be the birthday of the presiding deity of the village temple or the memory of a major event like the killing of a demon by the goddess.
[Contains English characters] The Vela falls on the 20th day of Meenam, the month in the Malayalam era .
[Contains English characters] Two competing groups, Nemmara and Vallangi, have their own temples plus a common temple, the Nellikkulangara, where the two groups can mingle.
[Contains English characters] The festivities start ten days earlier than the actual day of Vela, with the hoisting of a flag, in the respective temples.
[Contains English characters] Natives are not supposed to leave the village once the flags have been raised.
[Contains English characters] The Nemmara group starts its Vela from the Mandam or Vela Mandam and the Vallangi from the Siva temple.
[Contains English characters] There are 11 to 15 elephants for each of the two groups.
[Contains English characters] These elephants are decorated and to the accompaniment of percussion instruments, are paraded through the main thoroughfares of the town.
[Contains English characters] In the evening, these groups reach the Nellikulangara temple.
[Contains English characters] There is an area of empty fields here, enough to accommodate a large crowd.
[Contains English characters] The festival attracts a lot of people not only from nearby, but also from the neighbouring districts of Trissur, Malappuram and from Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] The Vela is also an occasion for family reunions.
[Contains English characters] People of the villages settled elsewhere, make it a point to attend the festival.
[Contains English characters] People celebrate this event as a whole without any discrimination of caste/religion.
[Contains English characters] Some foreign tourists are also usually seen.
[Contains English characters] Many TV channels broadcast the festival live.
[Contains English characters] Another attraction of the festival is the Aana Pandal which is an arch-like structure, where the caparisoned elephants remain for some time.
[Contains English characters] The Pandal, fully decorated with coloured electric lamps, give out different light patterns when switched on.
[Contains English characters] Both groups keep the design of the illuminations a secret.
[Contains English characters] The switching on of the Pandal on the previous day of the festival is a grand occasion for the local people.
[Contains English characters] The finale of the festival is the fireworks display.
[Contains English characters] It is a magnificent show, with both sides vying to get the upper hand.
[Contains English characters] New techniques are tried every year to bring out the best performance.
[Contains English characters] The quality and quantity of the fireworks are discussed by the people for many days after the event.
[Contains English characters] The selection of the elephants is another prestigious issue for the organisers.
[Contains English characters] They compete to get the best elephants in Kerala, paying exorbitant sums.
[Contains English characters] Both sides, are very competitive.
[Contains English characters] Sometimes, they try to get the same elephant, resulting in unrealistic bidding.
[Contains English characters] If the Nemmara have 21 elephants, the Vallengi will try to match that or have more and vice versa.
[Contains English characters] Various folk arts like Kummatti, Karivela and Andivela and so on, mark the next few days.
[Contains English characters] The Pothundy Dam is 6 km from Nemmara and is a stopping point for visitors to the Nelliyampathy hills.
[Contains English characters] Nearest Airport: Kochi or CoimbatoreNearest railway station: Palakkad or Trichur or Kollengode.
[Contains English characters] From Kochi Airport: travel to Trichur - 30 km, take a taxi to Nemmara or by bus from Trichur bus stand to Nemmara - 48 km.
[Contains English characters] From Coimbatore Airport : By Taxi or bus to Palakkad - 60 km.
[Contains English characters] From Palakkad: By taxi or bus to Nemmara, 28 km.
