[Contains English characters] साचा:माहितीचौकट Ethnic group तमिळ लोक किंवा तमिळ माणसं Tamil people also called Tamils or Tamilians, are a linguistic group native to Tamil Nadu, a state in India and the north-eastern region of श्रीलंका.
[Contains English characters] They speak Tamil, with a recorded history going back two millennia.
[Contains English characters] Emigrant communities are found across the world, notably Malaysia, Canada, Singapore, and the UK.
[Contains English characters] The Tamils are mostly Hindus with sizable Christian and Muslim populations.
[Contains English characters] Tamil was the first Indian language to be given classical status.
[Contains English characters] It has the oldest extant literature amongst other Dravidian languages.
[Contains English characters] The art and architecture of the Tamil people encompass some of the notable contributions of India and South-East Asia to the art world.
[Contains English characters] The famous Nataraja sculpture became a universal symbol of Hinduism.
[Contains English characters] The music, the temple architecture and the stylised sculptures favoured by the Tamil people in their ancient nation are still being learnt and practiced.
[Contains English characters] Thus, Tamils have been referred to as the last surviving classical civilisation on Earth.
[Contains English characters] The Pallava script, a variant of Southern Brahmi used by the Tamil Pallava dynasty, was the basis of several of the writing systems of Southeast Asia, including the Burmese, Khmer, Thai, Lao and Javanese scripts.
[Contains English characters] It is unknown as to whether the term Tamilar and its equivalents in Prakrit such as Damela, Dameda, Dhamila and Damila was a self designation or a term denoted by outsiders.
[Contains English characters] Epigraphic evidence of an ethnic group termed as such is found in ancient Sri Lanka where a number of inscriptions have come to light datable from third to first century BCE mentioning Damela or Dameda persons.
[Contains English characters] In the well-known Hathigumpha inscription of the Kalinga ruler Kharavela, refers to a Tramira samghata dated to 150 BCE.
[Contains English characters] It also mentions that the league of Tamil kingdoms had been in existence 113 years before then.
[Contains English characters] In Amaravati in present day Andhra Pradesh there is an inscription referring to a Dhamila-vaniya datable to the third century CE.
[Contains English characters] Another inscription of about the same time in Nagarjunakonda seems to refer to a Damila.
[Contains English characters] A third inscription in Kanheri Caves refers to a Dhamila-gharini .
[Contains English characters] In the Buddhist Jataka story known as Akiti Jataka there is a mention to Damila-rattha .
[Contains English characters] Hence it is clear that by at least the third century BCE, the ethnic identity of Tamils has been formed as a distinct group.
[Contains English characters] Tamilar is etymologically related to Tamil, the language spoken by Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] Southworth suggests that the name comes from tam-miz > tam-iz self-speak, or ones own speech.
[Contains English characters] Zvelebil suggests an etymology of tam-iz, with tam meaning self or ones self, and -iz having the connotation of unfolding sound.
[Contains English characters] Alternately, he suggests a derivation of tamiz < tam-iz < *tav-iz < *tak-iz, meaning in origin the proper process .
[Contains English characters] Possible evidence indicating the earliest presence of Tamil people in modern day Tamil Nadu are the megalithic urn burials, dating from around 1500 BC and onwards, which have been discovered at various locations in Tamil Nadu, notably in Adichanallur in Tirunelveli District which conform to the descriptions of funerals in classical Tamil literature.
[Contains English characters] Various legends became prevalent after the tenth century CE regarding the antiquity of the Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] According to Iraiyanar Agapporul, a tenth/eleventh-century annotation on the Sangam literature, the Tamil country extended southwards beyond the natural boundaries of the Indian peninsula comprising 49 ancient nadus .
[Contains English characters] The land was supposed to have been destroyed by a deluge.
[Contains English characters] The Sangam legends also added to the antiquity of the Tamil people by claiming tens of thousands of years of continuous literary activity during three Sangams.
[Contains English characters] From around the third century BC onwards, three royal dynasties—the Cholas, the Cheras and the Pandyas—rose to dominate the ancient Tamil country.
[Contains English characters] Each of these dynasties had its own realm within the Tamil-speaking region.
[Contains English characters] Classical literature and inscriptions also describe a number of Velirs, or minor chieftains, who collectively ruled over large parts of central Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] Wars between the kings and the chieftains were frequent, as were conflicts with ancient श्रीलंका.
[Contains English characters] These wars appear to have been fought to assert hegemony and demand tribute, rather than to subjugate and annex those territories.
[Contains English characters] The kings and chieftains were patrons of the arts, and a significant volume of literature exists from this period.
[Contains English characters] The literature shows that many of the cultural practices that are considered peculiarly Tamil date back to the classical period.
[Contains English characters] Agriculture was important during this period, and there is evidence that irrigation networks were built as early as 2nd century AD.
[Contains English characters] Internal and external trade flourished, and evidence exists of significant contact with Ancient Rome.
[Contains English characters] Large quantities of Roman coins and signs of the presence of Roman traders have been discovered at Karur and Arikamedu.
[Contains English characters] There is also evidence that at least two embassies were sent to the Roman Emperor Augustus by Pandya kings.
[Contains English characters] Potsherds with Tamil writing have also been found in excavations on the Red Sea, suggesting the presence of Tamil merchants there.
[Contains English characters] An anonymous first century travelers account written in Greek, Periplus Maris Erytraei, describes the ports of the Pandya and Chera kingdoms in Damirica and their commercial activity in great detail.
[Contains English characters] Periplus also indicates that the chief exports of the ancient Tamils were pepper, malabathrum, pearls, ivory, silk, spikenard, diamonds, sapphires, and tortoiseshell.
[Contains English characters] The classical period ended around the fourth century AD with invasions by the Kalabhra, referred to as the kalappirar in Tamil literature and inscriptions.
[Contains English characters] These invaders are described as evil kings and barbarians coming from lands to the north of the Tamil country.
[Contains English characters] This period, commonly referred to as the Dark Age of the Tamil country, ended with the rise of the Pallava dynasty.
[Contains English characters] According to Clarence Maloney, during the classical period Tamils also settled the Maldive Islands.
[Contains English characters] Although the Pallava records can be traced from the second century AD, they did not rise to prominence as an imperial dynasty until the sixth century.
[Contains English characters] The dynasty does not appear to have been Tamil in origin, although they rapidly adopted the local culture and the Tamil language.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas sought to model themselves after great northern dynasties such as the Mauryas and Guptas.
[Contains English characters] They therefore transformed the institution of the kingship into an imperial one, and sought to bring vast amounts of territory under their direct rule.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas were followers of the Hinduism, though for a short while one of their kings embraced Jainism and later converted to Hinduism.
[Contains English characters] The Bhakti movement in Hinduism was founded by Tamil saints at this time, and rose along with the growing influence of Jainism and Buddhism.
[Contains English characters] The Pallavas pioneered the building of large, ornate temples in stone which formed the basis of the Dravidian temple architecture.
[Contains English characters] The Pallava dynasty was overthrown in the 9th century by the resurgent Cholas.
[Contains English characters] The Cholas become dominant in the 10th century and established an empire covering most of southern India and Sri Lanka.
[Contains English characters] The empire had strong trading links with China and Southeast Asia.
[Contains English characters] The Cholas navy conquered the South Asian kingdom of Sri Vijaya in Sumatra and continued as far as Thailand and Burma.
[Contains English characters] Chola power declined in the 12th and 13th centuries, and the Pandya dynasty enjoyed a brief period of resurgence thereafter during the rule of Sundara Pandya.
[Contains English characters] However, repeated Muslim invasions from the 15th century onwards placed a huge strain on the empires resources, and the dynasty came to an end in the 16th century.
[Contains English characters] The western Tamil lands became increasingly politically distinct from the rest of the Tamil lands after the Chola and Pandya empires lost control over them in the 13th century.
[Contains English characters] They developed their own distinct language and literature, which increasingly grew apart from Tamil, evolving into the modern Malayalam language by the 15th century.
[Contains English characters] No major empires arose thereafter, and parts of Tamil Nadu were for a while ruled by a number of different local chiefs, such as the Nayaks of the modern महाराष्ट्र and Andhra Pradesh regions.
[Contains English characters] From the 17th century onwards, European powers began establishing settlements and trading outposts in the region.
[Contains English characters] A number of battles were fought between the British, French and Danish in the 18th century, and by the end of the 18th century most of Tamil Nadu was under British rule.
[Contains English characters] There is little scholarly consensus over the presence of the Tamil people in Sri Lanka, also known as Eelam in early Tamil literature, prior to the medieval Chola period .
[Contains English characters] One theory states that there was not an organized Tamil presence in Sri Lanka until the invasions from what is now South India in the 10th century AD; another theory contends that Tamil people were the original inhabitants of the island.
[Contains English characters] The indigenous Veddhas are physically related to Dravidian language-speaking tribal people in South India and early populations of Southeast Asia, although they no longer speak their native languages.
[Contains English characters] It is believed that cultural diffusion, rather than migration of people, spread the Sinhalese and Tamil languages from peninsular India into an existing Mesolithic population, centuries before the Christian era.
[Contains English characters] Settlements of people culturally similar to those of present-day Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu in modern India were excavated at megalithic burial sites at Pomparippu on the west coast and in Kathiraveli on the east coast of the island, villages established between the 5th century BC and 2nd century AD.
[Contains English characters] Cultural similarities in burial practices in South India and Sri Lanka were dated by archeologists to 10th century BC.
[Contains English characters] However, Indian history and archaeology have pushed the date back to 15th century BC, and in Sri Lanka, there is radiometric evidence from Anuradhapura that the non-Brahmi symbol-bearing black and red ware occur at least around 9th or 10th century BC.
[Contains English characters] Potsherds with early Tamil writing from the 2nd century BC have been found in excavations in Poonagari, Jaffna, bearing several inscriptions including a clan name - vela, a name related to velir from ancient Tamil country.
[Contains English characters] There is epigraphic evidence of people identifying themselves as Damelas or Damedas in Anuradhapura, the capital city of Rajarata, and other areas of Sri Lanka as early as the 2nd century BC.
[Contains English characters] Historical records establish that Tamil kingdoms in modern India were closely involved in the islands affairs from about the 2nd century BC.
[Contains English characters] In Mahavamsa, a historical poem, ethnic Tamil adventurers such as Elara invaded the island around 145 BC.
[Contains English characters] Tamil soldiers from what is now South India were brought to Anuradhapura between the 7th and 11th centuries AD in such large numbers that local chiefs and kings trying to establish legitimacy came to rely on them.
[Contains English characters] By the 8th century AD there were Tamil villages collectively known as Demel-kaballa, Demelat-valademin, and Demel-gam-bim .
[Contains English characters] In the 9th and 10th centuries AD, Pandya and Chola incursions into Sri Lanka culminated in the Chola annexation of the island, which lasted until the latter half of the 11th century CE.
[Contains English characters] The decline of Chola power in Sri Lanka was followed by the restoration of the Polonnaruwa monarchy in the late 11th century AD.
[Contains English characters] In 1215, following Pandya invasions, the Tamil-dominant Arya Chakaravarthi dynasty established an independent Jaffna kingdom on the Jaffna peninsula and parts of northern Sri Lanka.
[Contains English characters] The Arya Chakaravarthi expansion into the south was halted by Alagakkonara, a man descended from a family of merchants from Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] He was the chief minister of the Sinhalese king Parakramabahu V .
[Contains English characters] Vira Alakeshwara, a descendant of Alagakkonara, later became king of the Sinhalese, but he was overthrown by the Ming admiral Cheng Ho in 1409 AD.
[Contains English characters] The Arya Chakaravarthi dynasty ruled over large parts of northeast Sri Lanka until the Portuguese conquest of the Jaffna Kingdom in 1619 AD.
[Contains English characters] The coastal areas of the island were taken over by the Dutch and then became part of the British Empire in 1796 AD.
[Contains English characters] The English sailor Robert Knox described walking into the island’s Tamil country in the publication An Historical Relation of the Island Ceylon, annotating some kingdoms within it on a map in 1681 CE.
[Contains English characters] Upon arrival of European powers from the 17th century CE, the Tamils separate nation was described in their areas of habitation in the northeast of the island.
[Contains English characters] The caste structure of the majority Sinhalese has also accommodated Hindu immigrants from South India since the 13th century AD.
[Contains English characters] This led to the emergence of three new Sinhalese caste groups: the Salagama, the Durava and the Karava.
[Contains English characters] The Hindu migration and assimilation continued until the 18th century AD.
[Contains English characters] British colonists consolidated the Tamil territory in southern India into the Madras Presidency, which was integrated into British India.
[Contains English characters] Similarly, the Tamil parts of Sri Lanka joined with the other regions of the island in 1802 to form the Ceylon colony.
[Contains English characters] They remained in political union with India and श्रीलंका after their independence, in 1947 and 1948 respectively.
[Contains English characters] When India became independent in 1947, Madras Presidency became the Madras State, comprising present-day Tamil Nadu, coastal Andhra Pradesh, northern केरळ, and the southwest coast of Karnataka.
[Contains English characters] The state was subsequently split along linguistic lines.
[Contains English characters] In 1953, the northern districts formed Andhra Pradesh.
[Contains English characters] Under the States Reorganization Act in 1956, Madras State lost its western coastal districts.
[Contains English characters] The Bellary and South Kanara districts were ceded to Mysore state, and केरळ was formed from the Malabar district and the former princely states of Travancore and Cochin.
[Contains English characters] In 1968, Madras State was renamed Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] There was some initial demand for an independent Tamil state following the adoption of the federal system.
[Contains English characters] However, the Indian constitution granted significant autonomy to the states, and protests by Tamils in 1963 led to the government adopting a new policy called the three language formula.
[Contains English characters] This has led to Tamils in India becoming increasingly satisfied with the federal arrangement, and there is very little support for secession or independence today.
[Contains English characters] In Sri Lanka, however, the unitary arrangement led to a growing belief among some Tamils of discrimination by the Sinhalese majority.
[Contains English characters] This resulted in a demand for federalism, which in the 1970s grew into a movement for an autonomous Tamil country.
[Contains English characters] The situation deteriorated into civil war in the early 1980s.
[Contains English characters] A ceasefire in effect since 2002 broke down in August 2006 amid shelling and bombing from both sides.
[Contains English characters] Today Tamils make up 18% of Sri Lankas population .
[Contains English characters] Most Indian Tamils live in the state of Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] Tamils are the majority in the union territory of Pondicherry, a former French colony.
[Contains English characters] Pondicherry is a subnational enclave situated within Tamil Nadu.
[Contains English characters] Tamils account for at least one-sixth of the population in Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
[Contains English characters] There are also Tamil communities in other parts of India.
[Contains English characters] Most of these have emerged fairly recently, dating to the colonial and post-colonial periods, but some—particularly the Hebbar and Mandyam Tamils of southern Karnataka, पुणे, महाराष्ट्र, Andhra Pradesh, Palakkad in केरळ, and Delhi — date back to at least the medieval period.
[Contains English characters] There are two groups of Tamils in Sri Lanka: the Sri Lankan Tamils and the Indian Tamils.
[Contains English characters] The Sri Lankan Tamils are descendants of the Tamils of the old Jaffna Kingdom and east coast chieftaincies called Vannimais.
[Contains English characters] The Indian Tamils are descendants of bonded laborers sent from Tamil Nadu to Sri Lanka in the 19th century to work on tea plantations.
[Contains English characters] Furthermore, there is a significant Tamil-speaking Muslim population in Sri Lanka; however, unlike Tamil Muslims from India, they are not ethnic Tamils and are therefore listed as a separate ethnic group in official statistics.
[Contains English characters] Most Sri Lankan Tamils live in the Northern and Eastern provinces and in the capital कोलंबो, whereas most Indian Tamils live in the central highlands.
[Contains English characters] Historically both groups have seen themselves as separate communities, although there is a greater sense of unity since 1980s.
[Contains English characters] In 1949, the United National Party government, which included G. G. Ponnambalam, leader of the Tamil Congress, stripped the Indian Tamils of their citizenship.
[Contains English characters] This was opposed by S. J. V. Chelvanayakam, the leader of Tamil nationalist Federal Party, and most Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] Under the terms of an agreement reached between the Sri Lankan and Indian governments in the 1960s, about 40 percent of the Indian Tamils were granted Sri Lankan citizenship, and many of the remainder were repatriated to India.
[Contains English characters] By the 1990s, most Indian Tamils had received Sri Lankan citizenship.
[Contains English characters] Significant Tamil emigration began in the 18th century, when the British colonial government sent many poor Tamils as indentured labourers to far-off parts of the Empire, especially Malaya, South Africa, Fiji, Mauritius and the Caribbean.
[Contains English characters] At about the same time, many Tamil businessmen also immigrated to other parts of the British Empire, particularly to Burma and East Africa.
[Contains English characters] Many Tamils still live in these countries, and the Tamil communities in Singapore, Reunion Island, Malaysia and South Africa have retained much of their culture and language.
[Contains English characters] Many Malaysian children attend Tamil schools, and a significant portion of Tamil children in Mauritius and Reunion are brought up with Tamil as their first language.
[Contains English characters] In Singapore, Tamil students learn Tamil as their second language in school, with English as the first.
[Contains English characters] To preserve the Tamil language, the Singapore government has made it an official language despite Tamils comprising only about 5% of the population, and has also introduced compulsory instruction of the language for Tamils.
[Contains English characters] Other Tamil communities, such as those in South Africa and Fiji, no longer speak Tamil as a first language, but still retain a strong Tamil identity, and are able to understand the language, while most elders speak it as a first language.
[Contains English characters] A large emigration also began in the 1980s, as Sri Lankan Tamils sought to escape the ethnic conflict there.
[Contains English characters] These recent emigrants have most often fled to ऑस्ट्रेलिया, युरोप, North America and Southeast Asia.
[Contains English characters] Today, the largest concentration of Tamils outside southern Asia is in Toronto, Canada.
[Contains English characters] Many young Tamil professionals from India have also immigrated to Europe and the United States in recent times in search of better opportunities.
[Contains English characters] These new immigrant communities have established cultural associations to protect and promote Tamil culture and language in their adopted homes.
[Contains English characters] Tamils have strong feelings towards the Tamil language, which is often venerated in literature as Tamil̲an̲n̲ai, the Tamil mother.
[Contains English characters] It has historically been, and to large extent still is, central to the Tamil identity.
[Contains English characters] Like the other languages of South India, it is a Dravidian language, unrelated to the Indo-European languages of northern India.
[Contains English characters] The language has been far less influenced by Sanskrit than the other Dravidian languages, and preserves many features of Proto-Dravidian, though modern-day spoken Tamil in Tamil Nadu, freely uses loanwords from Sanskrit and English.
[Contains English characters] Tamil literature is of considerable antiquity, and is recognised as a classical language by the government of India.
[Contains English characters] Classical Tamil literature, which ranges from lyric poetry to works on poetics and ethical philosophy, is remarkably different from contemporary and later literature in other Indian languages, and represents the oldest body of secular literature in South Asia.
[Contains English characters] Notable works in classical Tamil literature include the Tirukkural, by Tiruvalluvar, the five great Tamil epics, and the works of Auvaiyar.
[Contains English characters] Modern Tamil literature is diverse.
[Contains English characters] It includes Indian Nationalism, in the works of Subramanya Bharathi; historical romanticism, by Kalki Krishnamurthy; radical and moderate social realism, by Pudhumaipithan and Jayakanthan; and feminism, by Malathi Maithri and Kutti Revathi.
[Contains English characters] Sujatha Rangarajan, an author whose works range from romance novels to science fiction, is one of the most popular modern writers in Tamil.
[Contains English characters] Sri Lankan Tamil literature has produced several works reflecting the civilian tragedy caused by decades of war.
[Contains English characters] There is also an emerging diaspora literature in Tamil.
[Contains English characters] There are a number of regional dialects in use by the Tamil people.
[Contains English characters] These dialects vary among regions and communities.
[Contains English characters] Tamil dialects are mainly differentiated by the disparate phonological changes and sound shifts that have evolved from Old Tamil.
[Contains English characters] Although most Tamil dialects do not differ significantly in their vocabulary, there are a few exceptions.
[Contains English characters] The dialects spoken in Sri Lanka retain many words that are not in everyday use in India, and use many other words slightly differently.
[Contains English characters] The dialect of the Iyers of Palakkad has a large number of Malayalam loanwords, has been influenced by Malayalam syntax, and has a distinct Malayalam accent.
[Contains English characters] The Sankethi, Hebbar, and Mandyam dialects, the former spoken by groups of Tamil Iyers, and the latter two by Vaishnavites who migrated to Karnataka in the 11th century, retains many Vaishnavite religious and spiritual values.
[Contains English characters] The Tamil spoken in चेन्नई infuses English words, and is called Madras Bashai .
[Contains English characters] Most traditional Tamil art is religious in some form and usually centres on Hinduism, although the religious element is often only a means to represent universal—and, occasionally, humanist—themes.
[Contains English characters] The most important form of Tamil painting is Tanjore painting, which originated in Thanjavur in the ninth century.
[Contains English characters] The paintings base is made of cloth and coated with zinc oxide, over which the image is painted using dyes; it is then decorated with semi-precious stones, as well as silver or gold thread.
[Contains English characters] A style which is related in origin, but which exhibits significant differences in execution, is used for painting murals on temple walls; the most notable example are the murals on the Kutal Azhakar and Meenakshi temples of Madurai, the Brihadeeswarar temple of Tanjore.
[Contains English characters] Tamil art, in general, is known for its stylistic elegance, rich colours, and attention to small details.
[Contains English characters] Tamil sculpture ranges from elegant stone sculptures in temples, to bronze icons with exquisite details.
[Contains English characters] The medieval Chola bronzes are considered to be one of Indias greatest contributions to the world art.
[Contains English characters] Unlike most Western art, the material in Tamil sculpture does not influence the form taken by the sculpture; instead, the artist imposes his/her vision of the form on the material.
[Contains English characters] As a result, one often sees in stone sculptures flowing forms that are usually reserved for metal.
[Contains English characters] As with painting, these sculptures show a fine eye for detail; great care is taken in sculpting the minute details of jewellery, worn by the subjects of the sculpture.
[Contains English characters] The lines tend to be smooth and flowing, and many pieces skillfully capture movement.
[Contains English characters] The cave sculptures at Mamallapuram are a particularly fine example of the technique, as are the bronzes of the Chola period.
[Contains English characters] A particularly popular motif in the bronzes was the depiction of Shiva as Nataraja, in a dance posture with one leg upraised, and a fiery circular halo surrounding his body.
[Contains English characters] Tamil temples were often simply treated as sculptures on a grand scale.
[Contains English characters] The temples are most notable for their high spires, known as Gopura, consisting of a number of stepped levels, and the vimanam, which rises above the sanctum sanctorum.
[Contains English characters] During the Chola period, the vimanams had more prominence, as seen in the Brihadīsvara temple of Thanjavur.
[Contains English characters] During the Nayak period, the spires became progressively more elaborate and ornate, as exemplified by the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai, while the vimanam became much smaller.
[Contains English characters] From the 13th century onwards, the entrance gates to the temples, called gopurams in Tamil, also began to grow bigger, and more elaborate.
[Contains English characters] The temples at Chidambaram and Srirangam have particularly impressive gopurams, covered with sculptures and reliefs of various scenes and characters from Hindu mythology.
[Contains English characters] As with Indian art in general, Tamil art does not traditionally aspire to portraiture or realism.
[Contains English characters] Much more emphasis is placed on the representation of ideal prototypes, and on depicting the symbols with which the theme of the artistic work is associated.
[Contains English characters] This means that small details, such as the direction which a hand faces, the animals or trees portrayed, or the time of day depicted, are often of critical importance to understanding the meaning of a work of art.
[Contains English characters] The traditional Tamil performing arts have ancient roots.
[Contains English characters] The royal courts and temples have been centres for the performing arts since the classical period, and possibly earlier.
[Contains English characters] Descriptions of performances in classical Tamil literature and the Natya Shastra, a Sanskrit treatise on the performing arts, indicate a close relationship between the ancient and modern artforms.
[Contains English characters] The aim of a performance in Tamil tradition, is to bring out the rasa, the flavor, mood, or feeling, inherent in the text, and its quality is measured by the extent to which it induces the mood in the audience.
[Contains English characters] Tamil shares a classical musical tradition, called carnatic music, with the rest of South India.
[Contains English characters] It is primarily oriented towards vocal music, with instruments functioning either as accompaniments, or as imitations of the singers role.
[Contains English characters] Ancient Tamil works, such as the Cilappatikaram, describe a system of music that includes old Carnatic modes, and a seventh-century Pallava inscription at Kudimiyamalai contains one of the earliest surviving examples of Indian music in notation.
[Contains English characters] Modern Carnatic music is organized around the twin notions of melody types, and cyclical rhythm types .
[Contains English characters] Unlike the northern Hindustani music tradition, carnatic music is almost exclusively religious.
[Contains English characters] In sharp contrast with the restrained and intellectual nature of carnatic music, Tamil folk music tends to be much more exuberant.
[Contains English characters] Popular forms of Tamil folk music include the Villuppattu, a form of music performed with a bow, and the Naattupurapaattu, ballads that convey folklore and folk history.
[Contains English characters] The dominant classical dance amongst Tamils is Bharatanatyam.
[Contains English characters] Bharatanatyam is performative, rather than participative.
[Contains English characters] The dance is an exposition of the story contained in a song, and is usually performed by one performer on stage, with an orchestra of drums, a drone, and one or more singers backstage.
[Contains English characters] The story is told through a complicated combination of mudras, facial expressions, and body postures.
[Contains English characters] Dancers used to be exclusively female, but the dance now also has several well-known male practitioners.
[Contains English characters] The most notable of Tamil folk dances is karakattam.
[Contains English characters] In its religious form, the dance is performed in front of an image of the goddess Mariamma.
[Contains English characters] The dancer bears, on his or her head, a brass pot filled with uncooked rice, decorated with flowers and surrounded by a bamboo frame, and tumbles and leaps to the rhythm of a song without spilling a grain.
[Contains English characters] Karakāṭṭam is usually performed to a special type of song, known as temmanguppattu, a folk song in the mode of a lover speaking to his beloved, to the accompaniment of a nadaswaram and melam.
[Contains English characters] Other Tamil folk dances include mayilattam, where the dancers tie a string of peacock feathers around their waists; oyilattam, danced in a circle while waving small pieces of cloth of various colors; poykkal kuthiraiyaattam, in which the dancers use dummy horses; manaattam, in which the dancers imitate the graceful leaping of deer; paraiyattam, a dance to the sound of rhythmical drumbeats; and thippanthattam, a dance involving playing with burning torches.
[Contains English characters] The kuravanci is a type of dance-drama, performed by four to eight women.
[Contains English characters] The drama is opened by a woman playing the part of a female soothsayer of the kurava tribe, who tells the story of a lady pining for her lover.
[Contains English characters] The therukoothu, literally meaning street play, is a form of village theater or folk opera.
[Contains English characters] It is traditionally performed in village squares, with no sets and very simple props.
[Contains English characters] The performances involve songs and dances, and the stories can be either religious or secular.
[Contains English characters] The performances are not formal, and performers often interact with the audience, mocking them, or involving them in the dialogue.
[Contains English characters] Therukkūthu has, in recent times, been very successfully adapted to convey social messages, such as abstinence and anti-caste criticism, as well as information about legal rights, and has spread to other parts of India.
[Contains English characters] The village of Melattur, in Tamil Nadu, has a special type of performance, called the bhagavata-mela, in honour of the local deity, which is performed once a year, and lasts all night.
[Contains English characters] Tamil Nadu also has a well developed stage theater tradition, which has been heavily influenced by western theatre.
[Contains English characters] A number of theatrical companies exist, with repertoires including absurdist, realist, and humorous plays.
[Contains English characters] Both classical and folk performing arts survive in modern Tamil society.
[Contains English characters] Tamil people in Tamil Nadu are also passionate about films.
[Contains English characters] The Tamil film industry, commonly dubbed Kollywood, is the second-largest film industry in India.
[Contains English characters] Tamil cinema is appreciated both for its technical accomplishments, and for its artistic and entertainment value.
[Contains English characters] Several actors dominated the early years of the cinema including Sivaji Ganesan, Gemini Ganesan, and several others.
[Contains English characters] As in the past, a small number of actors continue to dominate in Kollywood movies.
[Contains English characters] Several Tamil actresses have made their mark very strong in Bollywood over the years and have often dominated the scene, such as Vyjayanthimala, Rekha Ganesan, the original golden girl Hema Malini,Meenakshi Sheshadri, Vidya Balan, and Sridevi.
[Contains English characters] The overwhelming majority of Tamil films contain song and dance sequences, and Tamil film music is a popular genre in its own right, often liberally fusing elements of carnatic, Tamil folk, North Indian styles, hip-hop, and heavy metal.
[Contains English characters] Famous music directors of the late 20th century included M. S. Viswanathan, Ilayaraaja, and A.
[Contains English characters] R. Rahman. About 88% of the population of Tamil Nadu are Hindus.
[Contains English characters] Muslims and Christians account for 6% and 5.5% respectively.
[Contains English characters] Most of the Christians are Roman Catholics.
[Contains English characters] The majority of Muslims in Tamil Nadu speak Tamil, with less than 40% reporting Urdu as their mother tongue.
[Contains English characters] Tamil Jains number only a few thousand now.
[Contains English characters] Atheist, rationalist, and humanist philosophies are also adhered by sizable minorities, as a result of Tamil cultural revivalism in the twentieth century, and its antipathy to what it saw as Brahminical Hinduism.
[Contains English characters] The most popular deity is Murugan, also known as Karthikeya, the son of Siva.
[Contains English characters] The worship of Amman, also called Mariamman, is thought to have been derived from an ancient mother goddess, is also very common.
[Contains English characters] Kan̲n̲agi, the heroine of the Cilappatikār̲am, is worshipped as Pattin̲i by many Tamils, particularly in श्रीलंका.
[Contains English characters] There are also many followers of Ayyavazhi in Tamil Nadu, mainly in the southern districts.
[Contains English characters] In addition, there are many temples and devotees of Vishnu, Siva, Ganapathi, and the other Hindu deities.
[Contains English characters] The most important Tamil festivals are Pongal, a harvest festival that occurs in mid-January, and Varudapirappu, the Tamil New Year, which occurs around mid-April.
[Contains English characters] Both are celebrated by almost all Tamils, regardless of religion.
[Contains English characters] The Hindu festival Deepavali is celebrated with fanfare; other local Hindu festivals include Thaipusam, Panguni Uttiram, and Adiperukku.
[Contains English characters] While Adiperukku is celebrated with more pomp in the Cauvery region than in others, the Ayyavazhi Festival, Ayya Vaikunda Avataram, is predominantly celebrated in the southern districts of Kanyakumari, Tirunelveli, and Thoothukudi.
[Contains English characters] In rural Tamil Nadu, many local deities, called aiyyan̲ārs, are thought to be the spirits of local heroes who protect the village from harm.
[Contains English characters] Their worship often centers around nadukkal, stones erected in memory of heroes who died in battle.
[Contains English characters] This form of worship is mentioned frequently in classical literature and appears to be the surviving remnants of an ancient Tamil tradition.
[Contains English characters] The Saivist sect of Hinduism is significantly represented amongst Tamils, more so among Sri Lankan Tamils, although most of the Saivist places of religious significance are in northern India.
[Contains English characters] The Alvars and Nayanars, who were predominantly Tamils, played a key role in the renaissance of Bhakti tradition in India.
[Contains English characters] In the 10th century, the philosopher Ramanuja, who propagated the theory of Visishtadvaitam, brought many changes to worshiping practices, creating new regulations on temple worship, and accepted lower-caste Hindus as his prime disciples.
[Contains English characters] Christianity is believed to have come to Tamil Nadu with the arrival of St.
[Contains English characters] Thomas the apostle, and the number of Tamil Christians grew during the colonial period.
[Contains English characters] Most Tamil Christians are Catholic and Protestant.
[Contains English characters] Islam started flourishing in Tamilnadu after the arrival of Sulthan Syed Ibrahim Shaheed, descendant of Prophet Muhammmad who came from Madinah, Saudi Arabia during 12th century.
[Contains English characters] His grave is found in Erwadi dargah in Ramanathapuram district.
[Contains English characters] Tamil Muslims are mostly either mainstream Sunni or Sufi.
[Contains English characters] Each geographical area where Tamils live has developed its own distinct variant of the common dishes plus a few dishes distinctly native to itself.
[Contains English characters] The Chettinad region, comprising of Karaikudi and adjoining areas, is known for both traditional vegetarian dishes, like appam, uthappam, paal paniyaram, and non-vegetarian dishes, made primarily using chicken.
[Contains English characters] Rice, the major staple food in most of Tamil, is usually steamed and served with about two to six accompanying items, which typically include sambar, dry curry, rasam, kootu, and thayir or moru .
[Contains English characters] Tiffin or Light meals usually include one or more of Pongal, Dosai, idli, Vadai along with sambar and Chutney is often served as either breakfast or as an evening snack.
[Contains English characters] Ghee Clarified butter called neyyi in Tamil, is used to flavor the rice when eaten with dhal or sambar, but not with curds or buttermilk.
[Contains English characters] Morkulambu, a dish which can be spiced with moru, is also popular with steamed rice.
[Contains English characters] Various martial arts including Kuttu Varisai, Varma Kalai, Silambam Nillaikalakki, Maankombukkalai and Kalarippayattu, are practised in Tamil Nadu and केरळ.
[Contains English characters] The weapons used include Silambam, Maankombukkalai, Yeratthai Mulangkol, Surul Pattai, Val Vitchi, and Yeretthai Val .
[Contains English characters] The ancient Tamil art of unarmed bullfighting, popular amongst warriors in the classical period, has also survived in parts of Tamil Nadu, notably Alanganallur near Madurai, where it is known as Jallikaṭṭu or mañcuviraṭṭu and is held once a year around the time of the Pongal festival.
[Contains English characters] The global spread of the Tamil diaspora has hindered the formation of formal pan-Tamil institutions.
[Contains English characters] The most important national institutions for Tamils have been the governments of the states where they live, particularly the government of Tamil Nadu and the government of Sri Lanka, which have collaborated in developing technical and scientific terminology in Tamil and promoting its use since the 1950s.
[Contains English characters] Politics in Tamil Nadu is dominated by the Self-respect movement, founded by E. V. Ramasami, popularly known as Periyar, to promote self-respect and rationalism, and to fight casteism and the oppression of the lowest castes.
[Contains English characters] Every major political party in Tamil Nadu bases its ideology on the Self-respect Movement, and the national political parties play a very small role in Tamil politics.
[Contains English characters] In श्रीलंका, Tamil politics was dominated by the federalist movements, led by the Federal Party, until the early 1980s.
[Contains English characters] In the 1980s, the political movement for self determination in an autonomous Tamil Eelam was largely succeeded by a violent military campaign conducted by several militant groups.
[Contains English characters] The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, which emerged as the most important force amongst these groups in the 1990s, controlled a third of Sri Lanka, and had attempted to establish its own government there.
[Contains English characters] In the 1960s, the government of Tamil Nadu held a World Tamil Conference, which has continued to meet periodically since then.
[Contains English characters] In 1999, a World Tamil Confederation was established to protect and foster Tamil culture and further a sense of togetherness amongst Tamils in different countries.
[Contains English characters] The Confederation has since adopted a Tamil flag and Tamil song to act as trans-national symbols for the Tamil people; the words on the flag quote the opening line of a poem by the classical poet Kanian Poongundranaar, and means Everyone is our kin; Everyplace is our home.

[Contains English characters] org websites states An ISNI is made up of 16 digits, the last character being a check character.
[Contains English characters] In display it is frequently shown with spaces.
[Contains English characters] The ISNI allows a single identity to be identified using a unique number.
[Contains English characters] This unique number can then be linked to any of the numerous other identifiers that are used across the media industries to identify names and other forms of identity.
[Contains English characters] An example of the use of such a number is the identification of a musical performer who is also a writer both of music and of poems.
[Contains English characters] Where he or she might currently be identified in many different databases using numerous private and public identification systems, under the ISNI system, he or she would have a single linking ISNI record.
[Contains English characters] The many different databases could then exchange data about that particular identity without resorting to messy methods such as comparing text strings.
[Contains English characters] An often quoted example in the English language world is the difficulty faced when identifying John Smith in a database.
[Contains English characters] While there may be many records for John Smith, it is not always clear which record refers to the specific John Smith that is required.
[Contains English characters] If an author has published under several different names or pseudonyms, each such name will receive its own ISNI.
[Contains English characters] ISNI can be used by libraries and archives when sharing catalogue information; for more precise searching for information online and in databases, and it can aid the management of rights across national borders and in the digital environment.
[Contains English characters] ORCID identifiers consist of a reserved block of ISNI identifiers for scholarly researchers and administered by a separate organisation.
[Contains English characters] Individual researchers can create and claim their own ORCID identifier.
[Contains English characters] The two organisations coordinate their efforts.
[Contains English characters] ISNI is governed by an International Agency, commonly known as the ISNI-IA.
[Contains English characters] This UK registered, not-for-profit company has been founded by a consortium of organisations consisting of the Confédération Internationale des Sociétés d´Auteurs et Compositeurs, the Conference of European National Librarians, the International Federation of Reproduction Rights Organisations, the International Performers Database Association, the Online Computer Library Center and ProQuest.
[Contains English characters] It is managed by directors nominated from these organisations and, in the case of CENL, by representatives of the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the British Library.
[Contains English characters] ISNI-IA uses an assignment system comprising a user interface, data-schema, disambiguation algorithms, and database that meets the requirements of the ISO standard, while also using existing technology where possible.
[Contains English characters] The system is based primarily on the Virtual International Authority File service, which has been developed by OCLC for use in the aggregation of library catalogues.
[Contains English characters] Access to the assignment system and database, and to the numbers that are generated as the output of the process, are controlled by independent bodies known as registration agencies.
[Contains English characters] These registration agencies deal directly with customers, ensuring that data is provided in appropriate formats and recompensing the ISNI-IA for the cost of maintaining the assignment system.
[Contains English characters] Registration agencies are appointed by ISNI-IA but will be managed and funded independently.
[Contains English characters] As of 2017-08-05 ISNI holds public records of over 9.41 million identities, including 8.757 million individuals and 654,074 organisations.

[Contains English characters] Pooram is an annual temple festival held in central Kerala after the summer harvest.
[Contains English characters] Most pooram festivals have at least one ornately decorated elephant being paraded in the procession taken out of the temple precincts.
[Contains English characters] However, there are some, such as Aryankavu Pooram near Shoranur and Machattu Thiruvanikavu Vela near Wadakkanchery that do not use the caparisoned elephant, instead go for stilted mannequins of horses or bullocks.
[Contains English characters] The most famous of all Poorams is the Thrissur Pooram.
[Contains English characters] Some other well-known pooram festivals are Arattupuzha-Peruvanam Pooram, Nenmara Vallangi Vela, Uthralikavu Pooram and Chinakkathoor Pooram.
[Contains English characters] A melam is a classical performance of different kind of musical instruments that are unique to Kerala and is something akin to the jazz.
[Contains English characters] The most traditional of all melams is called Pandi Melam which is generally performed outside the temple, during the festival.
[Contains English characters] Another kind of melam is called Panchari Melam, which is similar to Pandi Melam going by the kind of instruments, but played inside the temple and following a different rhythmic beat.
[Contains English characters] Panchavadyam is another classical musical ensemble performed in Kerala.
[Contains English characters] Here, five different kinds of instruments create a breathtaking and fastmoving percussion performance.
[Contains English characters] The five instruments are Madhalam, Kombu, Edakka, Elathalam and Timila.
[Contains English characters] Thayambaka is a solo Chenda performance, where the performer uses one stick and the other hand to play the instrument instead of the usual two sticks.
[Contains English characters] Interesting attractions of Pooram can be seen in the Valluvanad and Talappilly region.
[Contains English characters] There is the Harijan Vela or Parayar Vela as well as the Tholpavakoothu, a traditional shadow puppetry show.

[Contains English characters] jQuery is free, open source software, licensed under the MIT License.
[Contains English characters] jQuerys syntax is designed to make it easier to navigate a document, select DOM elements, create animations, handle events, and develop Ajax applications.
[Contains English characters] jQuery also provides capabilities for developers to create plug-ins on top of the JavaScript library.
[Contains English characters] This enables developers to create abstractions for low-level interaction and animation, advanced effects and high-level, theme-able widgets.
[Contains English characters] The modular approach to the jQuery library allows the creation of powerful dynamic web pages and web applications.
[Contains English characters] The set of jQuery core features—DOM element selections, traversal and manipulation—enabled by its selector engine, created a new programming style, fusing algorithms and DOM-data-structures.
[Contains English characters] This style influenced the architecture of other JavaScript frameworks like YUI v3 and Dojo, later stimulating the creation of the standard Selectors API.

[Contains English characters] It is also possible to include jQuery directly from content delivery networks.

[Contains English characters] V-Day is a global movement to end violence against women and girls inspired by Eve Enslers play, योनी मनीच्या गुजगोष्टी .
[Contains English characters] The movement was started in the late 1990s by author, playwright and activist Eve Ensler.
[Contains English characters] Ensler has been quoted as saying that it was womens reactions to the play that launched V-Day.
[Contains English characters] After seeing योनी मनीच्या गुजगोष्टी, women would line up after to tell Eve their personal experiences, most often of sexual violence.
[Contains English characters] In 1998, a non-profit charity, V-Day, was incorporated with the intent of using performances of योनी मनीच्या गुजगोष्टी to raise money to benefit female victims of violence and sexual abuse.
[Contains English characters] Since its inception, the movement has expanded its use of art and activism to include film — most notably the documentary Until The Violence Stops, readings of the compilation A Memory, Monologue, A Rant, and a Prayer, marches, and festivals such as UNTIL THE VIOLENCE STOPS: NYC .
[Contains English characters] Beginning in early 2001, V-Day activities expanded to a host of international activities, with V-Day hosting leadership summits for women in Afghanistan, an international gathering of activists worldwide in Rome in September 2002, launching the Karama program in the Middle East, and more.
[Contains English characters] In some societies where the original monologues are considered too vulgar, such as Monte Carlo, Monaco, V-Day events revolve around the book A Memory, a Monologue, a Rant, and a Prayer, a collection of monologues written by acclaimed writers, at the request of Ensler to celebrate the plays tenth anniversary.
[Contains English characters] V-Day included the first ever all transgender version of योनी मनीच्या गुजगोष्टी in 2004, with a performance by eighteen notable transwomen under the mentoring of Jane Fonda and Andrea James of Deep Stealth Productions.
[Contains English characters] In 2008, over 3700 V-Day benefit events have been held or planned.
[Contains English characters] These events are being coordinated by volunteer activists in over 1250 locations around the world, educating millions of people about the reality of violence against women and girls.
[Contains English characters] According to www. vday. org, V-Days vision is a world where women live safely and freely.
[Contains English characters] V-Day demands that rape, incest, battery, genital mutilation and sexual slavery end immediately and believes that women should spend their lives creating and thriving rather than surviving or recovering from terrible atrocities.
[Contains English characters] The organization strives to unify and strengthen existing anti-violence efforts by raising money and consciousness, and to lay the groundwork for new educational, protective, and legislative endeavors throughout the world.
[Contains English characters] There are two types of V-Campaigns: The College Campaign and the Community Campaign.
[Contains English characters] The V-Day College Campaign engages members of college and university communities around the world to present benefit productions of योनी मनीच्या गुजगोष्टी, A Memory, A Monologue, A Rant and A Prayer, Until the Violence Stops, Any One of Us, and What I Want My Words to Do to You on their campuses to raise money and awareness to stop violence against women and girls.
[Contains English characters] The V-Day Community Campaign invites communities around the world to present productions of योनी मनीच्या गुजगोष्टी, A Memory, A Monologue, A Rant and A Prayer, Until the Violence Stops, Any One of Us, and What I Want My Words to Do to You to raise money and awareness to stop violence against women and girls.
[Contains English characters] Each year V-Day spotlights a particular group of women who are experiencing violence with the goal of raising awareness and funds to put a worldwide media spotlight on this area and to raise funds to aide groups who are addressing it.
[Contains English characters] The 2009 spotlight focuses on the women and girls from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
[Contains English characters] V-Day has attracted considerable critcism for hijacking the occasion of valentines day.
[Contains English characters] Critics argue that feminists should not be admonishing people to consider rape, incest and violence on an occasion designed to celebrate love and romance.
[Contains English characters] Feminist Wendy McElroy stated that V-Day embodies the same double standard and dishonesty that has characterized most feminist pronouncements for decades and urged people to take back Valentines Day.
[Contains English characters] Glenn Sacks criticised V-Day for being misandrist and for causing division between the genders, stating Valentines Day, which in the past symbolized the romantic bonds between men and women, has been turned into a day which further separates them.

[Contains English characters] साचा:Relatedसाचा:Two other uses Cooperation, co-operation, or coöperation is the process of working or acting together, which can be accomplished by both intentional and non-intentional agents.
[Contains English characters] In its simplest form it involves things working in harmony, side by side, while in its more complicated forms, it can involve something as complex as the inner workings of a human being or even the social patterns of a nation.
[Contains English characters] It is the alternative to working separately in competition.
[Contains English characters] Cooperation can also be accomplished by computers, which can handle shared resources simultaneously, while sharing processor time.
[Contains English characters] Cooperation, more formally speak is how the components of a system work together to achieve the global properties.
[Contains English characters] In other words, individual components that appear to be “selfish” and independent work together to create a highly complex, greater-than-the-sum-of-its-parts system.
[Contains English characters] Examples can be found all around us.
[Contains English characters] The components in a cell work together to keep it living.
[Contains English characters] Cells work together and communicate to produce multicellular organisms.
[Contains English characters] Organisms form food chains and ecosystems.
[Contains English characters] People form families, gangs, cities and nations.
[Contains English characters] Neurons create thought and consciousness.
[Contains English characters] Atoms cooperate in a simple way, by combining to make up molecules.
[Contains English characters] Understanding the mechanisms that create cooperating agents in a system is one of the most important and least well understood phenomena in nature, though there has not been a lack of effort.
[Contains English characters] However, cooperation may be coerced, voluntary, or even unintentional, and consequently individuals and groups might cooperate even though they have almost nothing in common qua interests or goals.
[Contains English characters] Examples of that can be found in market trade, military wars, families, workplaces, schools and prisons, and more generally any institution or organisation of which individuals are part .
[Contains English characters] Even if all members of a group would benefit if all cooperate, individual self-interest may not favor cooperation.
[Contains English characters] The prisoners dilemma codifies this problem and has been the subject of much research, both theoretical and experimental.
[Contains English characters] Results from experimental economics show that humans often act more cooperatively than strict self-interest would seem to dictate.
[Contains English characters] One reason for this may be that if the prisoners dilemma situation is repeated, it allows non-cooperation to be punished more, and cooperation to be rewarded more, than the single-shot version of the problem would suggest.
[Contains English characters] It has been suggested that this is one reason for the evolution of complex emotions in higher life forms, who, at least as infants, and usually thereafter, cannot survive without cooperating – although with maturation they gain much more choice about the kinds of cooperation they wish to have.
